S.R.O. 20.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution 
and in supersession of the Army Ordnance Corps, Civilian Staff Officer (Stores) Group ‘A’ post 
Recruitment Rules, 207, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, 
the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Civilian 
Staff Officer (Stores) in the Army Ordnance Corps, Ministry of Defence, namely: - 


l. Short title and commencement.— (|) These rules may be called the Army Ordnance Corps, Civilian 
Staff Officer (Stores), Group ‘A’ Post, Recruitment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix.— The number of the said post, its 
classification and level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the 
Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etec— The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (/3) of the 
said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification.— No person ,— 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the 
personal law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds 
for so doing, exempt any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to 
do, it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public 
Service Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of 
persons. 


6. Saving.— Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backword Classes, the 
Ex-servicemen and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central 
Government from time to time in this regard.

supersession of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Syce Recruitment 
Rules, 209, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby 
makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Syce in the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel 
National Police Academy, Hyderabad under the Ministry of Home Affairs, namely:- 


. Short title and commencement .— () These rules may be called the Ministry of Home Affairs, Sardar Vallabhbhai

rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, educational qualifications, etc-—— The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (3) of the said 
Schedule. 


4. Disqualification.— No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for doing so, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order, and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class 
or category of persons. 


6. Saving.— Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the other backward classes, the ex-Servicemen and other 
special categories of person, in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or

shall be eligible for appointment to the above said post:

person from the operation of this rule.

may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any 
class or category of persons.

be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, ex-servicemen and other 
special categories of persons, in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in 
this regard.

G.S.R. 30.— In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the National Institute of Communicable Disease Delhi Junior Translator (Hindi) Recruitment Rules, 
988, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the 
following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Junior Translation Officer in the National Centre 
for Disease Control under the Directorate General of Health Service, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
namely:- 


l. Short title and commencement. - (!) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare, National Centre for Disease Control, Junior Translation Officer (Group ‘B’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of the said post, its classification 
and level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to 
these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc. - The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (/3) of the said 
Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.- Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons.

G.S.R. 3l.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the National Institute of Communicable Diseases (Group ‘C’ Posts) Recruitment Rules, !980, in so 
far as they relate to the post of Senior Laboratory Assistant / Laboratory Assistant, except as respects things done or 
omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of 
recruitment to the post of Laboratory Assistant, in the National Centre for Disease Control under the Directorate 
General of Health Service, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, namely:- 


.Short title and commencement. - 


(.) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, National Centre for Disease 
Control, Laboratory Assistant (Group ‘C’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix .- The number of the said post, its classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to 
these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (/3) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualifications. - No person, - 


(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, 
exempt any person from the operation of this rule. 


5... Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to 
do, it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with 
respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, the ex- 
servicemen and the other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central 
Government from time to time in this regard.

required to be provided for the Schedule Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, ex-servicemen 
and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to 
time in this regard.

2. As per the claim statement, petitioner has averred that she was working under the control of the 
stn Respondent institution since 237 August 2000, as Mali in the Horticulture Department, and has been 
discharging her duties without complaint from any corer. Further, it is averred that the Respondents 1, to 
3 have been paying salary to the petitioner as per the salary statement. Therefore, there was an employer- 
employee relationship between the petitioner and Respondents | to 3. Respondents have been paying salary 
to the petitioner through middlemen, until 2011. Thereafter, Respondent has paid salary to Petitioner 
directly as per salary statement was prepared and signed by Estate officers, which is enclosed herein to 
substantiate the fact that the employer-employee relationship existed between the petitioner and 
Respondents | to 3 herein since September 2011. Further, the petitioner averred that the Respondents has 
paid salary directly to the petitioner till the end of May 2015, and again Respondents 1 to 3 have 
introduced middlemen from June 2015 onwards for the payment of the salaries to the petitioner. The mode 
of payment of wages is one of the conditions of service mentioned in Schedule IV of the ID Act, and 
under Section 9-A, it is mandated that no employer who proposes to effect any change in the conditions of 
service applicable to any workman in respect of any matter specified in the 4" Schedule, shall effect such 
change without giving to the workman any notice in the prescribed manner of the nature of the change 
proposed to be effected. Further, it is submitted that this action of the Respondent is in contravention of 
Section 9-A of the I.D Act and vide and initio in eyes of law. 


3: Further, Petitioner submitted that Respondents 1 to 3 have no power to change the service 
conditions under Section 9-A of the Act, and 47 Respondent has no power to terminate the service of the 
petitioner vide proceeding dated 8.9.2015, ordering the termination of the service of the petitioner. 
Therefore, action of Respondent No.4 issuing order of termination dated 8" September 2015 is null and 
void and liable to be said aside. Further, petitioner submitted that the Respondents | to 4 herein are bound 
to comply with Chapter V- B of the Industrial Disputes Act, in as much as since September 2011 the 
petitioner is under direct control of Respondents | to 3 herein, and Respondents 1 to 4 are bound to follow 
the procedure prescribed under Chapter V-B of the 1. Act. Further, it is submitted that Respondent has 
terminated the service of Petitioner without following the procedure as prescribed under of Section 25-B 
and 25-F of the ID Act. The termination order is not sustainable and contrary to the provision of the ID 
Act. Therefore, petitioner has prayed to set aside the order dated 08.09.2015 of her termination issued by 
the Respondent and to direct the Respondent to reinstate petitioner into service with continuity of service 
with all attendant benefits and full back wages. 


4. Notices were issued to Respondents. In response to the notice, Respondents 1 to 3 have filed 
counter. Despite service of notice Respondent 4 did not file any counter and case was set ex-parte against 
Respondent No. 4 by order dated 24" August 2017. Further, Respondent No. 1 to 3 did not appear on the 
date of hearing. Hence, case was proceeded ex-parte against Respondents 1 to 3 vide order dated 
19.12.2019. Therefore, hearing of this case has been proceeded ex-parte and being decided after conclusion 
of hearing.

5. In support of averment of claim statement petitioner has filed chief statement affidavit and therein, 
Petitioner has deposed that she was working as a casual labour under the control of the first Respondent 
institution since 237 August 2000 as a mali in the Horticulture department and was discharging her duties

officer that is enclose herein to substantiate the fact that an employer-employee relationship existed 
between the petitioner and Respondents 1 to 3 since September 2011. Further, deponent state that 
Respondent has paid the salary to the Petitioner directly till end of May 2015 and thereafter introduced the 
middleman from June 2015 onward. Deponent states that Respondent, without complying with the 
mandatory condition of issuing a notice for change in the condition of service under section 9-A of the I.D 
Act, has introduced the middleman and the action of the Respondent is illegal. Further, deponent states that

7. On going oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner in support of her claim 
document. Ex. W1/1 to Ex. W1/22 is the salary statements of the petitioner, which goes to reveal that

petitioner A. Lakshmi. Therein, it is mentioned that Respondent No.4 have received the letter from 
N.I.M.H for reducing the Horticulture labor, hence forth the services of the addressee is not required from 
the date mentioned therein. Thus, from the perusal of document, Ex. WS it is established that Petitioner had 
worked with the Respondent No. | to 3 as a Horticulture labour from September 2011 to 8.09.2015 and her 
services has been terminated vide letter dated 8.9.2015. Thus, it is clearly established that the petitioner had 
worked with the Respondent No. | to 3 as a casual labour continuously since September 2011 up to the 
date of termination i,e 08.09.2015 and she has been paid wages by Respondent No.1 to 3. 


Section 25F of the I.D Act, provides condition precedent for retrenchment of the workman. The 
provision is extracted as here under: - 


“25-F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen. ---No workman employed in any industry 
who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched 


by that employer until 


(a) The workman has been given one month’s notice in writing indicating the reasons for 
retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such 
notice, wages for the period of the notice: 


(b) The workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent 
to fifteen days’ average pay {for every completed year of continuous service} or any part thereof in 
excess of six months: and 


(c) Notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate government {or such authority as 
may be specified by the appropriate government by notification in the official Gazette.’

8. Thus, as per provision contained under section 25-F of I.D Act, before termination of Petitioner 
from service Respondent has not given one month notice to the Petitioner in writing indicating reasons for 
retrenchment or workman has not been paid in lieu of such notice wages for the period of notice. Further, 
Respondent has not paid compensation to the workman as per provision of the section 25F of Act. 


Therefore, the action of Respondent in terminating the services of workman Petitioner is in contravention 
of provision of section 25-F of I.D Act, and same is liable to be set aside. 


9. Thus, ongoing oral and documentary evidence produced by Petitioner it is established that 
Petitioner workman had worked with the Respondent No. 1 to 3 from September 2011 to 08.09.2015 
continuously and Petitioner has been terminated in contravention of provision of Section 25-F of I.D Act.

adduced by the Petitioner remains uncontroverted and unchallenged and there is no reason to disbelieve the 
evidence of the petitioner. Therefore, the evidence of the petitioner is liable to be accepted and it is proved 
that termination order dated 08.09.2015 of the Petitioner from service is illegal and that is liable to be set 
aside.

The claim of the petitioner is allowed. The termination order dated 08.09.2015 of the petitioner A. Laxmi

publication of order. Respondent No. 110 3 are also directed to pay the half back wages, to the petitioner 
from the date of her termination till the reinstatement of Petitioner.

3. The Petitioner union has filed claim statement with the prayer that the respondent management 
be directed to promote TH.M.L. Narayana, STS, (0) Eluru as_ per the rule. In the claim statement 
Petitioner has alleged that the workman, T.H.M.L. Narayana, STS, (O) is an employee working at Eluru 
under the Respondent management, and Respondent management is under obligation to upgrade the 
Confidential Reports of the T.H.M.L. Narayana, STS,(O) Eluru, and same to be communicated to the 
employees concerned to improve his performance. But Respondent management has not communicated the 
entry of ACR to every employee in compliance of the judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Devdutt 
Vs Union of India. The non-communication of entry in the ACR of employees is arbitrary and as such 
violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India, and also depriving the applicant from making a 
representation against it, which has, in turn, affected the chances of the applicant being promoted. 


Further, Petitioner has averred that in the year 2011, police has arrested T.Ms Viz., Sri B. Ram 
Mohan Rao, M. Appa Rao, M. Surya Rao, T. Durga Rao, Md. Rehman Sharif, K.S. Srinivas Rao, D. 
Venkat Rao, and Satya Prasad, as they were indulge in playing cards while on duty. After the arrested they 
were produced before the court for their criminal activities. All of the workman accused conferred before 
the court and they were imposed a fine of = 200 each, and all of them paid the fine. Further, it is alleged 
that when the said matter came into the knowledge of the respondent management, a show cause notice 
was issued to all the workmen, calling for explanation and after submitting their explanations, they were 
transferred to different rural telephone exchanges, as shown in the single transfer order dated 17" August 
2011, as a punishment. Further, it is alleged that one of the workmen, Shri K. S. Srinivas Rao, who is a 
member of Recognized Union BSNL ENIS, was brought back to an urban telephone exchange, while 
others were not brought back, as they belong to an unrecognized union. Further, it is alleged that the action 
of Respondent management in transferring the workmen to rural telephone exchanges as a punishment is 
illegal, in operative, and against the provision of law. The action of the Respondent management in 
considering the transfer of K. S. Srinivas Rao, TM, to an urban telephone exchange, being a member of a 
recognized union, is also illegal and untenable, as such is a biased attitude on the part of the Respondent 
management. Therefore, prayed to set aside the order of transfer of the remaining seven workmen to urban 
telephone exchanges in the interest of justice. 


Further, Petitioner has alleged that the respondent management is showing undue favor to the 
recognized union, flouting their own instructions issued from time to time. The Respondent management at 
Eluru had issued a circular dated 19 March 2008 to all the unions functioning in their organization, 
advising them not to conduct agitational programs within the premises of the office of the General 
Manager Telecom District, West Godavari, Eluru, followed by a reminder circular dated 29 November 
2012. In spite of these instructions, the recognized union continues to conduct agitational programs within 
the office premises. The half of the unrecognized unions brought this fact to the notice of the respondent 
management for taking instant action against the said recognized union, but the Respondent management 
was lukewarm to such an appeal. Therefore, Petitioner prayed that the management may be suitably 
punished for its partisan attitude shown to the unrecognized union in the interest of justice. 


4. Per contra, the Respondent has filed counter, and therein has denied all the material allegations 
made in the claim statement, except that are admitted here, and contended that petitioner is put to strict 
proof of the same. Further, Respondent contended that the ACRS of Shri TH. M. L. Narayana, STS, SO, 
Eluru, has been upgraded, and the official has been granted his first any PP on 17 October 2004, and 
second any PP on 1* October 2011, and the grievances of the said employee were settled on 20" May 
2015. Further, Respondent contended that Respondent denies the allegation of the claim statement 
regarding the change of transfer of Shri K. Srinivas Rao, TM, in favor of BSNL EU, as it is not true and 
correct. It is submitted that a vacancy existed to the place, 1.e., Anantapalli, where Shri K. S. Srinivas Rao, 
TM, requested a change of posting and transfer order was modified, as there was no vacancy available at 
that point time at the place Tadikalapudi and Aadamalli, as required by Shri T. Durga Rao, TM, Eluru and 
his request could not be considered to the said places. Respondent denied each of the material allegations 
made by the petitioner in claim statement in this regard. Further, it is contended that the Respondent 
department has circulated the office letter dated 29'-11- 2012 to all unions associations to prohibit any kind 
of holding of meetings or dharnas inside the office premises. The Respondent has specifically denied the 
allegation of favoritism to the recognized union against the rule, and each of such material allegations 
made by the petitioner. 


6942 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


On the basis of pleadings of both the parties, the following issues arise for determination: - 
1. Whether the demand of the workman of BSNL Eluru is legal and justified? 
2. To what other relief if any workmen are entitled? 
Findings:- 
Issue No.I: - 


As per claim statement petitioner has alleged that, due to non-upgradation of confidential report of 
T. H. M. L. Narayana, HS, TS, he could not be promoted, whereas respondent management is under 
obligation to upgrade the confidential reports of workman. In support of this allegation, petitioner has filed 
the chief evidence affidavit of witness WWI K. S. R. Murthy. Where in witness has reiterated the 
averment of claim statement. But, despite sufficient opportunity, this witness WW1 did not turn up for 
cross-examination. Therefore, the opportunity to produce the evidence was closed by the court vide order 
of 8" February 2023. As per law evidence for the want of cross-examination, the evidence of WW1 cannot 
be read in evidence. Petitioner did not adduce any other evidence to substantiate the allegation of claim 
statement. However, the Respondent, has contended that the ACR of Sri T. H. M. L. Narayana, S. T. S. (O) 
Eluru, has been upgraded, and he has been granted the first N E P P and second N E P P, and the grievance 
of the employee was settled on 207 May 2015. In support of this contention, the Respondent has also filed 
the copy of order dated 20" May 2015, issued by S. D. E. H. R., whereby the ACR of T. H. M. L. 
Narayana has been upgraded, and workman has been granted the first N E P P on 17 October 2004, and the 
second N E P P on 1* October 2011, and the case of the workman has been closed. Therefore, the 
grievances of the workman have been meet out vide order dated 20" May 2015, by the Respondent. 


Regarding rest of allegation of the petitioner, that the workman, who had been transferred as a 
punishment, their transfer orders are illegal, against the law. In this context, Petitioner has failed to prove 
any evidence on record to prove that the transfer orders, issued by the Respondent of these workman, vide 
order dated 17" August 2011, was motivated by personal bias, grudge, or improper motive. Further, the 
petitioner workman failed to prove that the transfer order dated 17" August 2011 has been issued in 
violation of certified standing orders or employment contract, or that it result in a change of service 
condition. Thus, petitioner has failed to discharge its burden of proof by adducing any positive evidence in 
this regard. Therefore, the allegation of the petitioner that their transfer was illegal is not tenable. Further, 
as regards the allegation of partial attitude towards the unrecognized union by the Respondent 
management, the petitioner failed to bring any cogent and reliable evidence on record so as to establish the 
plea partisan attitude toward Petitioner union being unrecognized as made in the claim statement. 
Therefore, in view of the foregoing discussion, I am of the considered opinion that the demand of the 
workman of BSNL Eluru is not legal and justified. 


The issue is decided against Petitioner. 
Issue No.II:- 


In view of the discussion and finding given at Issue No. I petitioner workman is not entitled to any 
relief and Petition is liable to be dismissed. 


AWARD 


In view of the finding on Issue No. 1 and I the demand of the workman of BSNL Eluru is not legal and 
justified. The claim statement filed by the petitioner is devoid of merit stands dismissed. The reference is 
answered accordingly.

AWARD 


This petition has been filed by the petitioner, Smt.Ch. Nagarani, against the Respondents, | to 4 
under Section 2(A)(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, with the prayer to set aside her termination 
order dated 31.08.2015 issued by Respondent No. 4. Further, it is prayed to direct the Respondents to 
reinstate the petitioner into service with continuity of service, with full back wages and all other attendant 
benefits. 


6950 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [Part II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


2. As per the claim statement, petitioner has averred that she was working under the control of the Ist 
Respondent institution since 2.05.2011, as Sweeper in housekeeping in the Horticulture Department, and 
has been discharging her duties without complaint from any corner. Further, it is averred that the 
Respondents 1, to 3 have been paying salary to the petitioner as per the salary statement. Therefore, there 
was an employer-employee relationship between the petitioner and Respondents 1 to 3. Respondents have 
been paying salary to the petitioner through middlemen, until 2011. Thereafter, Respondent has paid salary 
to Petitioner directly as per salary statement was prepared and signed by Estate officers, which is enclosed 
herein to substantiate the fact that the employer-employee relationship existed between the petitioner and 
Respondents | to 3 herein since September 2011. Further, the petitioner averred that the Respondents has 
paid salary directly to the petitioner till the end of May 2015, and again Respondents 1 to 3 have 
introduced middlemen from June 2015 onwards for the payment of the salaries to the petitioner. The mode 
of payment of wages is one of the conditions of service mentioned in Schedule IV of the ID Act, and 
under Section 9-A, it is mandated that no employer who proposes to effect any change in the conditions of 
service applicable to any workman in respect of any matter specified in the 4" Schedule, shall effect such 
change without giving to the workman any notice in the prescribed manner of the nature of the change 
proposed to be effected. Further, it is submitted that this action of the Respondent is in contravention of 
Section 9-A of the I.D Act and vide and initio in eyes of law. 


3. Further, Petitioner submitted that Respondents 1 to 3 have no power to change the service 
conditions under Section 9-A of the Act, and 47 Respondent has no power to terminate the service of the 
petitioner vide proceeding dated 31.08.2015, ordering the termination of the service of the petitioner. 
Therefore, action of Respondent No.4 issuing order of termination dated 31.08.2015 is null and void and 
liable to be said aside. Further, petitioner submitted that the Respondents 1 to 4 herein are bound to comply 
with Chapter V- B of the Industrial Disputes Act, in as much as since September 2011 the petitioner is 
under direct control of Respondents 1 to 3 herein, and Respondents 1 to 4 are bound to follow the 
procedure prescribed under Chapter V-B of the I.D Act. Further, it is submitted that Respondent has 
terminated the service of Petitioner without following the procedure as prescribed under of Section 25-B 
and 25-F of the ID Act. The termination order is not sustainable and contrary to the provision of the ID 
Act. Therefore, petitioner has prayed to set aside the order dated 31.08.2015 of her termination issued by 
the Respondent and to direct the Respondent to reinstate petitioner into service with continuity of service 
with all attendant benefits and full back wages. 


4. Notices were issued to Respondents. In response to the notice, Respondents 1 to 3 have filed 
counter. Despite service of notice Respondent 4 did not file any counter and case was set ex-parte against 
Respondent No. 4 by order dated 24 August 2017. Further, Respondent No. 1 to 3 did not appear on the 
date of hearing. Hence, case was proceeded ex-parte against Respondents 1 to 3 vide order dated 
19.12.2019. Therefore, hearing of this case has been proceeded ex-parte and being decided after conclusion 
of hearing. 


De In support of averment of claim statement petitioner has filed chief statement affidavit and therein, 
Petitioner has deposed that she was working as a casual labour under the control of the first Respondent 
institution since 237 August 2000 as Sweeper in housekeeping in the Horticulture department and was 
discharging her duties without any complaint from any corner. Further, petitioner deposed that, since 2011 
onward, her salary has been paid directly by Respondents 1 to 3, and salary statement was prepared and 
signed by the Estate officer that is enclose herein to substantiate the fact that an employer-employee 
relationship existed between the petitioner and Respondents 1 to 3 since September 2011. Further, 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 6951 


deponent state that Respondent has paid the salary to the Petitioner directly till end of May 2015 and 
thereafter introduced the middleman from June 2015 onward. Deponent states that Respondent, without 
complying with the mandatory condition of issuing a notice for change in the condition of service under 
section 9-A of the I.D Act, has introduced the middleman and the action of the Respondent is illegal. 
Further, deponent states that Respondent has terminated her service in gross violation of the provision 
contained under chapter V of the I.D Act, as enshrined within the meaning of sections 25-B and 25-F of the 
I.D Act. 


6. Further, petitioner has also exhibited documents in her testimony in support of her averment made 
in claim statement. These documents are Ex. W1 is the salary statement of the petitioner issued by the 3rd 
Respondent. Ex. W2 is the conciliation proceedings of the Assistant Labor Commissioner, Hyderabad. Ex. 
W3, the RTI application dated 13°°2015. Ex. W4, the RTI information furnished by the second 
Respondent. Ex. W5 is the termination order and Ex. W6 is the letter of the petitioner union to RLC(C) 
dated 09.09.2015. 


if On going oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner in support of her claim 
document. Ex. W1/1 to Ex. W1/22 is the salary statements of the petitioner, which goes to reveal that 
petitioner Smt. Ch. Nagarani had worked with the Respondent No. 110 3 continuously from 02.05.2011 on 
casual basis up to the date of her termination and she has been paid wages as per number of working days 
month wise by the Respondent No. 110 3 Estate Officer. The termination order dated 31.08.2015 Ex. W5 
that goes to show that the Respondent No. 4 had issued the termination order, dated 31.08.2015 of the 
petitioner Ch. Nagarani Therein, it is mentioned that Respondent No.4 have received the letter from 
N.I.M.H for reducing the Horticulture labor, hence forth the services of the addressee is not required from 
the date mentioned therein. Thus, from the perusal of document, Ex. WS it is established that Petitioner had 
worked with the Respondent No. | to 3 as a Horticulture labour from September 2011 to 31.08.2015 and 
her services has been terminated vide letter dated 31.08.2015. Thus, it is clearly established that the 
petitioner had worked with the Respondent No. | to 3 as a casual labour continuously since 02.05.2011 up 
to the date of termination i,e 31.08.2015 and she has been paid wages by Respondent No.1 to 3. 


Section 25F of the I.D Act, provides condition precedent for retrenchment of the workman. The 
provision is extracted as here under: - 


“25-F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen. ---No workman employed in any industry 
who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched 


by that employer until 


(a) The workman has been given one month’s notice in writing indicating the reasons for 
retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such 


notice, wages for the period of the notice: 


(b) The workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent 
to fifteen days’ average pay {for every completed year of continuous service} or any part thereof in 
excess of six months: and 


(c) Notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate government {or such authority as 


d 


may be specified by the appropriate government by notification in the official Gazette.’ 


6952 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


8. Thus, as per provision contained under section 25-F of I.D Act, before termination of Petitioner 
from service Respondent has not given one month notice to the Petitioner in writing indicating reasons for 
retrenchment or workman has not been paid in lieu of such notice wages for the period of notice. Further, 
Respondent has not paid compensation to the workman as per provision of the section 25F of Act. 
Therefore, the action of Respondent in terminating the services of workman Petitioner is in contravention 
of provision of section 25-F of I.D Act, and same is liable to be set aside. 


9. Thus, ongoing oral and documentary evidence produced by Petitioner it is established that 
Petitioner workman had worked with the Respondent No. | to 3 from 02.05.2011 to 31.08.2015 
continuously and Petitioner has been terminated in contravention of provision of Section 25-F of I.D Act. 
Further it is established that Respondent No. | to 3 has changed the condition of services of Petitioner 
without complying the provision of section 9-A of the I.D Act. The oral and documentary evidence 
adduced by the Petitioner remains uncontroverted and unchallenged and there is no reason to disbelieve the 
evidence of the petitioner. Therefore, the evidence of the petitioner is liable to be accepted and it is proved 
that termination order dated 31.08.2015 of the Petitioner from service is illegal and that is liable to be set 
aside. 


AWARD 


The claim of the petitioner is allowed. The termination order dated 31.08.2015 of the petitioner Smt. Ch. 
Nagarani from service issued by the Respondent is hereby set aside. Respondent No. 1 to 3 is directed to 
reinstate the petitioner into service, with continuity and all attendant benefits within in one-month from 
date of publication of order. Respondent No. | to 3 are also directed to pay the half back wages, to the 
petitioner from the date of her termination till the reinstatement of Petitioner. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.

AWARD 


This petition has been filed by the petitioner, Sri. Ch. Sambaiah, against the Respondents, 1 to 4 
under Section 2(A)(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, with the prayer to set aside his termination 
order dated 31.08.2015 issued by Respondent No. 4. Further, it is prayed to direct the Respondents to 
reinstate the petitioner into service with continuity of service, with full back wages and all other attendant 
benefits. 


2: As per the claim statement, petitioner has averred that he was working under the control of the 17 
Respondent institution since August 2009, as Sweeper in housekeeping in the Horticulture Department, 
and has been discharging his duties without complaint from any corner. Further, it is averred that the 
Respondents 1, to 3 have been paying salary to the petitioner as per the salary statement. Therefore, there 
was an employer-employee relationship between the petitioner and Respondents 1 to 3. Respondents have 
been paying salary to the petitioner through middlemen, until 2011. Thereafter, Respondent has paid salary 
to Petitioner directly as per salary statement was prepared and signed by Estate officers, which is enclosed 
herein to substantiate the fact that the employer-employee relationship existed between the petitioner and 


[भाग I—ave 3(ii)] भारत का UAT : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 6955 


Respondents | to 3 herein since September 2011. Further, the petitioner averred that the Respondents has 
paid salary directly to the petitioner till the end of May 2015, and again Respondents 1 to 3 have 
introduced middlemen from June 2015 onwards for the payment of the salaries to the petitioner. The mode 
of payment of wages is one of the conditions of service mentioned in Schedule IV of the ID Act, and 
under Section 9-A, it is mandated that no employer who proposes to effect any change in the conditions of 
service applicable to any workman in respect of any matter specified in the 4 Schedule, shall effect such 
change without giving to the workman any notice in the prescribed manner of the nature of the change 
proposed to be effected. Further, it is submitted that the action of the Respondent is in contravention of 
Section 9-A of the I.D Act and vide and initio in eyes of law. 


3. Further, Petitioner submitted that Respondents 1 to 3 have no power to change the service 
conditions under Section 9-A of the Act, and 47 Respondent has no power to terminate the service of the 
petitioner vide proceeding dated 31.08.2015, ordering the termination of the service of the petitioner. 
Therefore, action of Respondent No.4 issuing order of termination dated 31.08. 2015 is null and void and 
liable to be said aside. Further, petitioner submitted that the Respondents 1 to 4 herein are bound to comply 
with Chapter V- B of the Industrial Disputes Act, in as much as since August 2009 the petitioner is under 
direct control of Respondents 1 to 3 herein, and Respondents 1 to 4 are bound to follow the procedure 
prescribed under Chapter V-B of the I.D Act. Further, it is submitted that Respondent has terminated the 
service of Petitioner without following the procedure as prescribed under of Section 25-B and 25-F of the 
ID Act. The termination order is not sustainable and contrary to the provision of the ID Act. Therefore, 
petitioner has prayed to set aside the order dated 31.08.2015 of his termination issued by the Respondent 
and to direct the Respondent to reinstate petitioner into service with continuity of service with all attendant 
benefits and full back wages. 


4. Notices were issued to Respondents. In response to the notice, Respondents | to 3 have filed 
counter. Despite service of notice Respondent 4 did not file any counter and case was set ex-parte against 
Respondent No. 4 by order dated 24" August 2017. Further, Respondent No. | to 3 did not appear on the 
date of hearing. Hence, case was proceeded ex-parte against Respondents 1 to 3 vide order dated 
19.12.2019. Therefore, hearing of this case has been proceeded ex-parte and being decided after conclusion 
of hearing. 


5. In support of averment of claim statement petitioner has filed chief statement affidavit and therein, 
Petitioner has deposed that he was working as a casual labour under the control of the first Respondent 
institution since 23™ August 2000 as Sewerage Treatment Plant in the Horticulture department and was 
discharging his duties without any complaint from any corner. Further, petitioner deposed that, since 2011 
onward, his salary has been paid directly by Respondents 1 to 3, and salary statement was prepared and 
signed by the Estate officer that is enclose herein to substantiate the fact that an employer-employee 
relationship existed between the petitioner and Respondents 1 to 3 since September 2011. Further, 
deponent state that Respondent has paid the salary to the Petitioner directly till end of May 2015 and 
thereafter introduced the middleman from June 2015 onward. Deponent states that Respondent, without 
complying with the mandatory condition of issuing a notice for change in the condition of service under 
section 9-A of the I.D Act, has introduced the middleman and the action of the Respondent is illegal. 
Further, deponent states that Respondent has terminated his service in gross violation of the provision 
contained under chapter V of the I.D Act, as enshrined within the meaning of sections 25-B and 25-F of the 
I.D Act.

6. Further, petitioner has also exhibited documents in his testimony in support of his averment made 
in claim statement. These documents are Ex. W1 is the salary statement of the petitioner issued by the 3rd 
Respondent. Ex. W2 is the conciliation proceedings of the Assistant Labor Commissioner, Hyderabad. Ex. 
W3, the RTI application dated 13°°2015. Ex. W4, the RTI information furnished by the second 
Respondent. Ex. W5 is the termination order and Ex. W6 is the letter of the petitioner union to RLC(C) 
dated 09.09.2015. 


re On going oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner in support of his claim 
document. Ex. W1/1 to Ex. W1/22 is the salary statements of the petitioner, which goes to reveal that 
petitioner Sri. Ch. Sambaiah had worked with the Respondent No. 110 3 continuously from August 2009 
on casual basis up to the date of his termination and he has been paid wages as per number of working days 
month wise by the Respondent No. 110 3 Estate Officer. The termination order dated 31.08.2015 Ex. W5 
that goes to show that the Respondent No. 4 had issued the termination order, dated 31.08.2015 of the 
petitioner Sri. Ch. Samabaiah. Therein, it is mentioned that Respondent No.4 have received the letter from 
N.I.M.H for reducing the Horticulture labor, hence forth the services of the addressee is not required from 
the date mentioned therein. Thus, from the perusal of document, Ex. WS it is established that Petitioner had 
worked with the Respondent No. 1 to 3 as a Horticulture labour from 2009 to 31.08.2015 and his services 
has been terminated vide letter dated 31.08.2015. Thus, it is clearly established that the petitioner had 
worked with the Respondent No. 110 3 as a casual labour continuously since August 2009 up to the date 
of termination i,e 31.08.2015 and he has been paid wages by Respondent No.1 to 3. 


Section 25F of the I.D Act, provides condition precedent for retrenchment of the workman. The 
provision is extracted as here under: - 


“25-F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen. ---No workman employed in any industry 
who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched 


by that employer until 


(a) The workman has been given one month’s notice in writing indicating the reasons for 
retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such 


notice, wages for the period of the notice: 


(b) The workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent 
to fifteen days’ average pay {for every completed year of continuous service} or any part thereof in 


excess of six months: and 


(c) Notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate government {or such authority as 


I 


may be specified by the appropriate government by notification in the official Gazette.’ 


8. Thus, as per provision contained under section 25-F of I.D Act, before termination of Petitioner 
from service Respondent has not given one month notice to the Petitioner in writing indicating reasons for 
retrenchment or workman has not been paid in lieu of such notice wages for the period of notice. Further, 
Respondent has not paid compensation to the workman as per provision of the section 25F of Act. 
Therefore, the action of Respondent in terminating the services of workman Petitioner is in contravention 
of provision of section 25-F of I.D Act, and same is liable to be set aside. 


9. Thus, ongoing oral and documentary evidence produced by Petitioner it is established that 
Petitioner workman had worked with the Respondent No. 1 to 3 from August 2009 to 31.08.2015 
continuously and Petitioner has been terminated in contravention of provision of Section 25-F of I.D Act. 


[भाग ए---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 6957 


Further it is established that Respondent No. | to 3 has changed the condition of services of Petitioner 
without complying the provision of section 9-A of the I.D Act. The oral and documentary evidence 
adduced by the Petitioner remains uncontroverted and unchallenged and there is no reason to disbelieve the 
evidence of the petitioner. Therefore, the evidence of the petitioner is liable to be accepted and it is proved 
that termination order dated 31.08.2015 of the Petitioner from service is illegal and that is liable to be set 
aside. 


AWARD 


The claim of the petitioner is allowed. The termination order dated 31.08.2015 of the petitioner Sri. 
Ch. Sambaiah from service issued by the Respondent is hereby set aside. Respondent No. | to 3 is directed 
to reinstate the petitioner into service, with continuity and all attendant benefits within in one-month from 
date of publication of order. Respondent No. | to 3 are also directed to pay the half back wages, to the 
petitioner from the date of his termination till the reinstatement of Petitioner. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.

Section 25F of the I.D Act, provides condition precedent for retrenchment of the workman. The

“25-F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen. ---No workman employed in any industry

to fifteen days’ average pay {for every completed year of continuous service} or any part thereof in

Ts On going oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner in support of her claim 
document. Ex. W1/1 to Ex. W1/22 is the salary statements of the petitioner, which goes to reveal that 
petitioner Smt. K. Lavanya had worked with the Respondent No. | to 3 continuously from September 2011 


on casual basis up to the date of her termination and she has been paid wages as per number of working

days month wise by the Respondent No. 110 3 Estate Officer. The termination order dated 31.08.2015 Ex. 
W5 that goes to show that the Respondent No. 4 had issued the termination order, dated 8.9.2015 of the 
petitioner K. Lavanya. Therein, it is mentioned that Respondent No.4 have received the letter from 
N.I.M.H for reducing the Horticulture labor, hence forth the services of the addressee is not required from 
the date mentioned therein. Thus, from the perusal of document, Ex. WS it is established that Petitioner had 
worked with the Respondent No. 1 to 3 as a Horticulture labour from June 2011 to 31.08.2015 and her 
services has been terminated vide letter dated 31.8.2015. Thus, it is clearly established that the petitioner 
had worked with the Respondent No. | to 3 as a casual labour continuously since June 2011 up to the date 


of termination i,e 31.08.2015 and she has been paid wages by Respondent No.1 to 3. 


Section 25F of the I.D Act, provides condition precedent for retrenchment of the workman. The 


provision is extracted as here under: - 


“25-F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen. ---No workman employed in any industry 
who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched 


by that employer until 


(a) The workman has been given one month’s notice in writing indicating the reasons for 
retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such 


notice, wages for the period of the notice: 


(b) The workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent 
to fifteen days’ average pay {for every completed year of continuous service} or any part thereof in 


excess of six months: and 


(c) Notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate government {or such authority as 


3 


may be specified by the appropriate government by notification in the official Gazette.’ 


8. Thus, as per provision contained under section 25-F of I.D Act, before termination of Petitioner 
from service Respondent has not given one month notice to the Petitioner in writing indicating reasons for 
retrenchment or workman has not been paid in lieu of such notice wages for the period of notice. Further, 
Respondent has not paid compensation to the workman as per provision of the section 25F of Act. 
Therefore, the action of Respondent in terminating the services of workman Petitioner is in contravention 


of provision of section 25-F of I.D Act, and same is liable to be set aside. 


9. Thus, ongoing oral and documentary evidence produced by Petitioner it is established that 
Petitioner workman had worked with the Respondent No. 1 to 3 from June 2011 to 31.08.2015 
continuously and Petitioner has been terminated in contravention of provision of Section 25-F of I.D Act. 
Further it is established that Respondent No. | to 3 has changed the condition of services of Petitioner 
without complying the provision of section 9-A of the I.D Act. The oral and documentary evidence 
adduced by the Petitioner remains uncontroverted and unchallenged and there is no reason to disbelieve the 
evidence of the petitioner. Therefore, the evidence of the petitioner is liable to be accepted and it is proved 
that termination order dated 31.08.2015 of the Petitioner from service is illegal and that is liable to be set 


aside.

month from date of publication of order. Respondent No. 1 to 3 are also directed to pay the half back 


wages, to the petitioner from the date of her termination till the reinstatement of Petitioner.

The Claim Statement has been filed by Smt. Janaki Basfore on 10-08-2021. The Management of 
Central Water Commission, (CWC), Middle Brahmaputra Division, Guwahati filed their Written Statement 
through Executive Engineer on 11-04-2022 but the same was incorporated in the record on 27-07-2022. 


The fact of the case according to the claim statement of the workman is that the workman, a casual 
worker of the Central Water Commission, (CWC) Middle Brahmaputra Division, Guwahati raised an 
Industrial Dispute against the Management of Central Water Commission, (CWC) Middle Brahmaputra 
Division, Guwahati for illegal termination from service and non-payment of arrear salary as well as current 
salary. It is stated that the workman was engaged as a casual Sweeper/Cleaner from 01-05-2006 to 24-06- 
2019 by the Central Water Commission, Middle Brahmaputra Division, Guwahati and she was thereafter 
engaged through Contractor firm namely M/S Challenger Detective, New Delhi w.e.f. 25-06-2019. It is 
stated that such engagement through a contractor firm was a paper arrangement only. The workman further 
stated that on 24-03-2020 lockdown was declared by the Government of Assam and CWC, Guwahati 
informed the workman not to come to office during lockdown period. When she went to attend her duty on 
16-04-2020, the Management of CWC, Guwahati informed her that her service had been terminated due to 
expiry of contract period of the Contractor. It is further stated that the contract of conservancy and 
sweeping/cleaning work was given to M/S BIPICIRI, Guwahati on 15-07-2020 for supply of contract 
workers and they supplied new workers in place of old workers who did not get any job opportunity. It is 
submitted that due to her long span of service, she is entitled to have her daily wages as 1/30" of the pay of 
the minimum scale as paid to the regular employee. It is submitted that termination of service of Smt. 
Janaki Basfore is neither legal nor justified without providing retracement compensation under section 25F 
of Industrial Dispute Act,1947. The workman also raised objection for change of her service condition 
from casual labour to a contractual labour. The workman has prayed for her reinstatement in service with 
all incidental benefits. 


Management of CWC contested the case by filing Written Statement, contending interalia that the 
workman is a casual worker appointed from time to time. In the year 2019-2020 the Management floated 
contract through Government-e-Marker (GeM) for outsourcing of four number of staff. M/S Challenger 
Detective, New Delhi was the lowest bidder and contract was awarded to the contractor firm for one year 
w.e.f. 24-06-2019 to 01-04-2020. It is stated that due to Covid pandemic, lockdown was declared from 25- 
03-2020 and the contract period expired on 01-04-2020, hence, the question of termination of the workman 
does not arise and Section 25F does not confer any right to the employee for her reinstatement and 


regularization of service. 


In the written statement, management further submitted that in respect of change of service 
condition of the workman, Section 9A of Industrial Dispute Act is applicable to workman in matters 
specified in the Fourth Schedule of the Act. According to the Management, workman was engaged under 
the Contractor firm from 24-06-2019 to 01-04-2020. After completion of the specified period fresh tender 
was issued and the claim regarding change of service condition of the petitioner was not applicable after 
expiry of period of contract. 


The Management of Central Water Commission, Middle Brahmaputra Division, Guwahati further 
contended that the workman was never given the status of casual worker and as such the demand for 
payment for 1/30th of pay at minimum pay scale as applicable to regular employees is not attracted to 
contractual employees. Management accordingly prayed for dismissal of the Industrial Dispute. 


Smt. Janaki Basfore filed her evidence-in-chief in support of her case wherein she stated that she 
joined her service on 01-04-2006 and she was terminated from service on 02-05-2020 without any reason

or notice. In her evidence on affidavit, she stated that her last drawn salary of Rs.8,105/- was credited to 
her Saving Bank Account No.35127405960 with State Bank of India, Pandu Port Branch, Guwahati. As 
per order dated 16-06-2025, the witness cannot be cross examined as she was unable to recollect the dates 


of her induction in employment and termination. 
Case is fixed up today during special campaign for disposal of old cases. 


As per last order dated 23-12-2025, fresh notices were issued to the parties under Speed post informing 
them that the case is fixed up today i.e. 03-02-2026. The Management is appeared through Mr. Amit 
Kurdia, Assistant Executive Engineer, Central Water Commission, Guwahati along with their engaged 
learned Advocate Mr. H. Gupta. Notice sent to Smt. Janaki Basfore has been returned unserved with postal 
report “No such person in this addressee”. Ex-parte order was already passed vide order dated 04-03-2021 
against the O.P. No.2 M/s BIPICIRI, Guwahati the Contractor. 


Record reveals that after filing evidence by the workman on 16.06.2025, the case was fixed up for 
cross examination of workman witness on several dates, but the workman did not appear. In this case the 
workman filed her evidence on affidavit but unable to recollect her date of joining as well as date of 


termination for which she was not cross examined. 


Considering the materials in the record, it appears to me that ample opportunity has been provided 
to the workman but she did not turn up. It is thus, abundantly clear that the workman is not interested to go 
ahead with the proceeding. She even did not appear for cross examination. As such her evidence-in-chief 
on affidavit cannot be considered. In the above, I find that the workman failed to establish her case. The 
Industrial Dispute is therefore disposed of without any relief. Let a no relief award be drawn up. 


ORDERED 


The Industrial dispute is dismissed. Let a no relief Award be drawn up. Copies of the Award in

Ram, Contract Worker w.e.f. 24.02.2020 from Security and Housekeeping work of National

case.’ 
On 06.07.2022 behalf of the respondent statement of defence was filed. 


Thereafter, workman filed rejoinder affidavit on 27.03.2023 and evidence in support of his cased vide 
affidavit dated 29.10.2022. 


After filing of the evidence on affidavit, in spite of several opportunities given to workman, he did not turn 


up for his cross-examination. 
In spite of notice to the workman that matter shall proceed ex-parte, none appeared on behalf of workman. 
Accordingly heard learned counsel for respondent, Sri Banwari Lal and gone through the records. 


It is clearly established that claimant/workman has filed evidence on affidavit in support of his case; but in 
spite of several opportunities did not turn up for her cross-examination by the respondent on evidence filed 
by him on affidavit in support of his case. 


Thus, it is a case of no evidence from the side of workman/claimant in support of his case, once he has not 
been cross-examined by the respondent. 


Keeping, in view of the above said facts as well as the law as laid by the Hon'ble High Court in the 
case of V. # Raj Industries v. Labour Court (1) and others 1981 (29) FLR 194 as under: 


“It is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him 
to prove illegality of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction 
of the Court must fail. Whenever a workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the 
termination of service if is imperative for him to file written statement before the Industrial 
Court setting out grounds on which the order is challenged and he must also produce 
evidence to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file written statement or 
produce evidence, the dispute referred by the State Government cannot be answered in 


favour of the workman and he would not be entitled to any relief.” 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding 
Officer, Labour Court (II), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (118) FLR 1164 Hon’ble Allahabad High Court 
has held as under: 


“The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia 
Biscuit Co. Ltd., V.K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. 
State of U.P. and Ors. 1984 (49) FLR 38 and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. 
1996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led by or on behalf of the workman the 
reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In such a situation it is 
not necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead evidence to 
establish an allegation made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would 


be, who would fail if no evidence is led.”

And by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. 
P.A.C.C.S.C. Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co-operative Bank Ltd. 2010 (126) FLR 519; 
wherein it has been held as under: 


“The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the 
shoulders of the respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to 
lead evidence first which he failed. A perusal of the impugned award also does not show 
that any evidence either oral or documentary was led by the respondent. In the case of no 


evidence, the reference has to be dismissed.” 


As the workman did not turn up for cross-examination, after submitting his evidence in support of his case, 
filed on affidavit (examination-in-chief), so it is a case of no evidence filed on behalf of workman in 
support of case set up by him, liable to be dismissed. 


For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and; and the workman is not entitled for any relief. 
Award as above.

"2. (00) "retrenchment" means the termination by the employer of the service of a workman for

25F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen.- 


No workman employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one

(a) the workman has been given one month's notice in writing indicating the reasons for

Further the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case of Sarita Tiwari Versus Aastha Garments reported in

"20. It is well-settled that the burden to prove that the workman was in continuous employment of 
240 days with the management is on the workman herself. This principle was reiterated by the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the landmark judgement of R.M. Yellatti v. Asstt. 


Executive Engineer, (2006) 1 SCC 106; the relevant paragraph is extracted below:- 


"17. Analysing the above decisions of this Court, it is clear that the provisions of the 
Evidence Act in terms do not apply to the proceedings under Section 10 of the Industrial 
Disputes Act. However, applying general principles and on reading the aforestated 
judgments, we find that this By: MANISH KUMAR W.P.(C) 5369/2019 8 of 16 Court has 
repeatedly taken the view that the burden of proof is on the claimant to show that he had 
worked for 240 days in a given year. This burden is discharged only upon the workman 
stepping in the witness box. This burden is discharged upon the workman adducing cogent 
evidence, both oral and documentary. In cases of termination of services of daily-waged 
earners, there will be no letter of appointment or termination. There will also be no receipt 
or proof of payment. Thus in most cases, the workman (the claimant) can only call upon 
the employer to produce before the court the nominal muster roll for the given period, the 
letter of appointment or termination, if any, the wage register, the attendance register, etc. 
Drawing of adverse inference ultimately would depend thereafter on the facts of each case. 
The above decisions however make it clear that mere affidavits or self-serving statements 
made by the claimant workman will not suffice in the matter of discharge of the burden 
placed by law on the workman to prove that he had worked for 240 days in a given year. 
The above judgments further lay down that mere non-production of muster rolls per se 
without any plea of suppression by the claimant workman will not be the ground for the 
Tribunal to draw an adverse inference against the management. Lastly, the above 
judgments lay down the basic principle, namely, that the High Court under Article 226 of 
the Constitution will not interfere with the concurrent findings of fact recorded by the 
Labour Court unless they are perverse. This exercise will depend upon the facts of each 


case." 


21. These principles were reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam

6. It was the case of the workman that he had worked for more than 240 days in the year

worked for 240 days in a given year. This burden is discharged only upon the workman

evidence, both oral and documentary. In cases of termination of services of daily-waged 
earners, there will be no letter of appointment or termination. There will also be no receipt 
or proof of payment. Thus in most cases, the workman (the claimant) can only call upon 
the employer to produce before the court the nominal muster roll for the given period, the 
letter of appointment or termination, if any, the wage register, the attendance register, etc. 
Drawing of adverse inference ultimately would depend thereafter on the facts of each case. 
The above decisions however make it clear that mere affidavits or self-serving statements 
made by the claimant workman will not suffice in the matter of discharge of the burden 
placed by law on the workman to prove that he had worked for 240 days in a given year.

without any plea of suppression by the claimant workman will not be the ground for the 
Tribunal to draw an adverse inference against the management. Lastly, the above 
judgments lay down the basic principle, namely, that the High Court under Article 226 of 
the Constitution will not interfere with the concurrent findings of fact recorded by the 
Labour Court unless they are perverse. This exercise will depend upon the facts of each 


case."

himself on the evidence filed by him on affidavit (examination in chief) so the same in not proved as per 


the relevant provision Evidence Act, so keeping the said facts and the law as laid by the Hon'ble High 
Court in the case of V. K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court (1) and others 1981 (29) FLR 194 as under: 


"It is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to 
prove illegality of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the 
Court must fail Whenever a workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of 
service if is imperative for him to file written statement before the Industrial Court setting out 
grounds on which the order is challenged and he must also produce evidence to prove his case. If 
the workman fails to appear or to file written statement or produce evidence, the dispute referred 
by the State Government cannot be answered in favour of the workman and he would not be 


entitled to any relief." 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees' Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. 
Presiding Officer, Labour Court ता), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (118) FLR 1164 Hon'ble Allahabad 
High Court has held as under: 


"The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit 
Co. Ltd., V.K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. 
and Ors. 1984 (49) FLR 38 and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1996 FLR that in the 
absence of any evidence led by or on behalf of the workman the reference is bound to be answered 
by the court against the workman. In such a situation it is not necessary for the employers to lead 
any evidence at all. The obligation to lead evidence to establish an allegation made by a party is 


on the party making the allegation. The test would be, who would fail if no evidence is led." 


And by the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. 
P.A.C.C.S.C. Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co- operative Bank Ltd. 2010 (126) FLR 519; 


wherein it has been held as under: 


"The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the 


shoulders of the respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to lead 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7015 


evidence first which he failed. A perusal of the impugned award also does not show that any 
evidence either oral or documentary was led by the respondent. In the case of no evidence, the 


reference has to be dismissed." 


AWARD 
For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and; and the workman is not entitled for any relief. 


Award as above.

Rs. 462/- per day.

since his appointment in June 2010. 


5. Apart from his work as a watchman/plumber, the applicant/labourer also did all the work given 
by the officials like running the water motor, carrying the dock and in the 3 LIC offices located

(111) Kindly provide the outstanding salary along with 18% interest from June 30, 2018 till 
today/date of the order.

favour of the applicant/labourer.

Industry nor such person working therein are workman as defined in Section 2 (s) of the 
Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. As such it is not an Industrial Dispute as defined in the Act. In 
view of these submissions the claim of the applicant Shri Yashin is not maintainable and is 
liable to be rejected.

wage basis on highly intermittent casual nature of work. The applicant Shri Yashin has himself 
stated that he worked some time as Plumber, some time as a watchman and some time as a

post or vacancy exists as such the applicant cannot be regularized.

filed on behalf of the claimant to support his claim, as such, the adjudication case is liable to be dismissed. 


Thus, taking into consideration the facts on record that in the present case the workman has not filed any

In view of the foregoing discussion and in the given circumstance the reference stands disposed of as of

Reference is answered accordingly. 


Parties are left to bear their respective costs.

AWARD 


The present proceedings arise pursuant to the remand orders passed by the Hon’ble High Court, whereby 
this Tribunal has been directed to determine the last drawn wages of the Workman as on 03.10.1996 for the 
purposes of Section 17-B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, during the pendency of the writ petition 
filed by the Employer challenging the Award passed in Complaint No. CGIT-1 of 2002 arising out of 
Reference No. CGIT-34 of 1996. 


In view of the directions of the Hon’ble High Court, the following issue arises for determination: 


“What were the last drawn wages of the Workman as on 03.10.1996 for the purposes of Section 17-B 
of the Industrial Disputes Act?” 


The Employer, being aggrieved by the Award in favour of the Workman, preferred Writ Petition No. 5700 
of 2006 before the Hon’ble High Court. During the pendency of the writ petition, the Workman filed an 
application under Section 17-B of the Industrial Disputes Act. 


The Employer initially computed the last drawn wages at Rs. 7,034/-, which was subsequently revised to 
Rs. 10,555/-. Both figures were disputed by the Workman. 


By order dated 05.09.2011 in Contempt Petition No. 7 of 2010, the Hon’ble High Court directed the parties 
to appear before this Tribunal for determination of the said issue. 


7028 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


This Tribunal, by order dated 07.03.2012, determined the wages at Rs. 10,555/-. The said order was 
challenged by the Workman in Writ Petition No. 5519 of 2012. The Hon’ble High Court, vide order dated 
07.10.2013, remanded the matter for fresh adjudication with specific directions. 


Directions of the Hon’ble High Court 


a. 


b. 


The Hon’ble High Court, by order dated 19.03.2013, directed the Employer to produce: 
Evolution of remuneration in the establishment; 

Details of bonus/ex gratia and other financial benefits; 

Computerized wage statements with full break-up of allowances. 


Despite lapse of considerable time, the said documents have not been produced before this 


Tribunal. 


Non-Compliance and Withholding of Evidence 


The Employer has taken a plea in its affidavit dated 25.09.2025 that the records are old and not 
traceable. This plea is vague and unsupported by any material particulars. 


It is a settled position of law that withholding of best evidence invites adverse inference. In Gopal 
Krishnaji Ketkar v. Mohamed Haji Latif, AIR 1968 SC 1413, the Hon’ble Supreme Court held 
that a party in possession of best evidence must produce it, failing which the Court is justified in 


drawing adverse inference. 


The same principle has been reiterated in Municipal Corporation, Faridabad v. Siri Niwas, 
(2004) 8 SCC 195, wherein it was held that non-production of relevant records by the employer 
justifies presumption against it. Likewise, in R.M. Yellatti v. Assistant Executive Engineer, 
(2006) 1 SCC 106, the Hon’ble Supreme Court held that failure to produce wage records entitles 
the Court to accept the workman’s version. 


The Employer’s selective production of documents is equally impermissible. In Ramchandra 
Keshav Adke v. Govind Joti Chavare, (1975) 1 SCC 559, it was held that where a thing is 


required to be done in a particular manner, it must be done in that manner alone. 


The Hon’ble Bombay High Court has also consistently held that an employer cannot avoid liability 
by withholding service records. In Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation v. 
Rajendra Bhimrao Mandve, 2001 (89) FLR 560 (Bom.), it was observed that failure to produce 


service records warrants adverse inference against the employer. 

Failure to Establish Pay Fixation 

The record shows that the Employer has failed to produce any documentary proof regarding: 
Fixation of initial pay; 

Pay revision in 1987 and 1992; 

Fixation upon promotion in 1990. 


In Sriram Industrial Enterprises Ltd. v. Mahak Singh, (2007) 4 SCC 94, the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court held that the employer, being custodian of records, must produce them, failing which 
adverse inference follows. 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7029 


It is also well settled that promotion must result in financial benefit. In Union of India v. P.N. 
Menon, (1994) 4 SCC 68, it was held that pay fixation must be lawful and rational. Similarly, in 
State of Punjab v. Jagjit Singh, (2017) 1 SCC 148, the Hon’ble Supreme Court emphasized that 
employees cannot be denied legitimate financial benefits. 


Effect of High Court Orders on Promotion 


The Minutes of Order dated 26.06.1996 passed by the Hon’ble High Court clearly granted notional 
promotion to the Workman from 01.01.1994. 


The Employer has failed to consider the said direction. Such conduct cannot be accepted. In 
Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation v. S.G. Kotturappa, (2005) 3 SCC 409, it was 
held that failure to comply with binding judicial directions disentitles a party from equitable relief. 


The Hon’ble Bombay High Court in Air India Ltd. v. Vishal V. Kshirsagar, 2009 (122) FLR 
121 (Bom.) has also emphasized that service benefits flowing from judicial orders must be duly 
reflected in wage computation. 


Section 17-B and Distinction from Dena Bank Case 


The Employer has relied upon Dena Bank v. Kirit Kumar T. Patel, (1999) 2 SCC 106. However, the 
said judgment relates to notional wages based on future revisions. 


In the present case, the Workman is claiming actual wages last drawn prior to termination. Hence, the 


said judgment is distinguishable. 


Section 17-B is a beneficial provision. In Workmen v. Hindustan Vegetable Oils Corporation Ltd., 
(2000) 9 SCC 632, the Hon’ble Supreme Court held that such provisions must be interpreted in favour 
of the workman. Similarly, in Bharat Singh v. Management of New Delhi Tuberculosis Centre, 
(1986) 2 SCC 614, it was held that technicalities should not defeat substantive justice. 


Appreciation of Evidence 
The Workman has filed a detailed affidavit establishing that his last drawn wages were Rs. 20,726/-. 
The Employer has failed to specifically deny the calculations. The reply is vague and evasive. 


In H.D. Singh v. Reserve Bank of India, (1985) 4 SCC 201, it was held that vague denials are no 
denials in the eyes of law. 


Principles of Social Justice 
The Workman, now aged about 76 years, has remained unemployed for nearly three decades. 


In Harjinder Singh v. Punjab State Warehousing Corporation, (2010) 3 SCC 192, the Hon’ble 
Supreme Court held that labour adjudication must be guided by social justice. Similarly, in Surendra 
Kumar Verma v. CGIT, (1980) 4 SCC 443, it was held that industrial adjudication must avoid 
technical rigidity. 

Findings 
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that: 
e The Employer has failed to comply with binding directions of the Hon’ble High Court; 
e The Employer has withheld best evidence; 


e The Workman’s claim is credible and remains uncontroverted.

AWARD 
Accordingly, it is held that: 


The last drawn wages of the Workman as on 03.10.1996 are Rs. 20,726/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand 
Seven Hundred Twenty Six only). 


The issue referred by the Hon’ble High Court stands answered accordingly. 
Directions 

The Employer is hereby directed to: 

Pay wages under Section 17-B on the basis of Rs. 20,726/-; 


Comply within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

AWARD
