The present application has been filed under Section 2-A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 
(hereinafter referred to as ‘the Act’). The claimant submits that he had been working with the 
management as an Electrician since 05.09.2008 and his last drawn salary was rupees 12,798/- per month. It 
is alleged that the management has been operating under different names, though the nature of work and 
workforce remain the same. The service record of the claimant was clean and unblemished, and no 
complaint was ever made against him. At the time of appointment, his signatures were obtained on blank 
papers, vouchers, and appointment letters, copies of which were never supplied to him. It is further alleged 
that he was deprived of statutory facilities such as attendance card, leave book, overtime wages, weekly 
and festival holidays, annual increments, and timely payment of wages. When the claimant demanded 
these, the managements became annoyed and withheld his earned wages for the period from 01.03.2017 to 
30.03.2017 and illegally terminated his services on 31.03.2017 in violation of Section 25F of the Act, 
without issuing notice, or following due procedure, despite the fact that he had worked for more than 240 
days in each year. Thereafter, the claimant approached the Labour Department and raised an industrial 
dispute before the Conciliation Officer, but due to non-cooperation of the management, the conciliation 
proceedings failed and a failure certificate under section 2A of the Act was issued by the appropriate 
government. The claimant asserts that he has remained unemployed since the date of termination despite 
best efforts and has no source of livelihood. He, therefore, prays that the termination be declared illegal and 
unjustified, and that he be reinstated in service with continuity and full back wages along with interest @ 


18% per annum. 


In response, the management filed its written statement opposing the claim of the workman. The 
management raised preliminary objections that the present claim petition is false, frivolous, and devoid of 
any cause of action, as it has been filed with the intention to harass the management and extract money by 
misusing the provisions of labour laws. It is stated that no industrial dispute exists as the claimant is not a 
“workman” within the meaning of the Act, and therefore, the claim is liable to be dismissed. It is further 
alleged that the claimant has not approached the Court with clean hands and has concealed material facts, 
he is a habitual litigant who has filed similar claims against other establishments despite being in 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7041 


continuous employment. The management also submits that it reserves its right to file an 
amended/additional written statement upon receipt of supporting documents. 


On merits, the management denies that the claimant was in service since 05.09.2008, stating 
instead that he was employed as an Electrician w.e.f. 01.04.2013 with last drawn wages of 211,500/- per 
month plus HRA of =1,298/-. It is denied that the management was operating under two different entities, 
clarifying that the company, presently known as Medsave Health Insurance TPA Limited, was earlier 
known as Medsave Healthcare TPA Limited and the name change was duly approved by the competent 
authorities. The management further denies that the claimant had a clean service record, alleging that he 
was irregular, negligent, and frequently absent without prior permission, for which he was repeatedly 
warned. It is also denied that any signatures were obtained on blank papers or that statutory facilities were 
not provided; rather, it is asserted that the management, being a professionally managed public limited 
company, complied with all applicable labour laws. 


The management specifically denies termination of services and asserts that the claimant 
voluntarily resigned vide letter dated 31.03.2017 on account of securing better employment and requested 
to release him immediately to join the new job on 01.04.2017, which was accordingly granted. It is stated 
that full and final settlement was prepared but the claimant failed to collect the same. The allegations of 
illegal termination and violation of Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 are denied. It is further 
contended that the management duly participated in conciliation proceedings and attempted settlement, but 
the claimant avoided accepting dues. The management disputes the claim of unemployment, asserting that 
the claimant is gainfully employed elsewhere, and further submits that the position vacated by him has 
already been filled, leaving no vacancy. Accordingly, it is contended that the claimant is not entitled to any 
relief, and the claim petition deserves to be dismissed. 


A rejoinder had also been filed by the claimant, where he denied the averments made by the 
management in its W.S. and reaffirmed the averments of his claim statement. However, he admitted to 
have resigned on 31.03.2017, though he asserted that the same had been obtained from him under threat to 
kill him. He further stated that on 15.04.2017, he addressed a letter to the management seeking withdrawal 
of his resignation. He also admitted that he had worked with M/s. Delhi Darbar Gastronomy Pvt. Ltd. 
during the period of his employment with the management, but clarified that the said job was on a part- 
time basis from 06:30 PM to 10:00 PM, whereas he worked with the management from 10:00 AM to 06:00 
PM. 


From pleadings of the party, following issues were framed vide order dated 20.05.2019. 
1. | Whether the proceeding is maintainable. 


2. | Whether the services of the workman were terminated illegally in violation of the provisions 
of the ID Act by the management. 


3. If the workman is entitled to reinstatement to service with back wages and interest on the 
back wages. 


4. 10 what other relief the workman is entitled to. 


In order to substantiate his claim, the claimant examined himself and reiterated the facts as stated 
in his claim statement as well as in the rejoinder. He relied upon seven documents, the seventh document is 
a marked document (Mark-1)’. The documents relied upon by the claimant are as follows: 


7042 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


1. Demand letter dated 15.04.2017 sent to the management. (WW1/1) 
2: Speed post receipt. (WW1/2) 


3. A letter written to the management dated 15.04.2017 seeking withdrawal of his resignation 
letter. (WW 1/3) 


4. A copy of identity card. (WW1/4) 


5. A copy of letter written by the management (dated 22.01.2024) verifying the claimant’s 
employment in their office. (WW1/5) 


6. A copy of appointment letter. (WW1/6) 


7. A copy of letter written by the management (dated 14.12.2011) verifying the claimant’s 
employment in their office. (Mark-1). 


The witness was put to the test of cross-examination, wherein he admitted that the resignation 
letter was written by him in his own handwriting, and bore his signature dated 31.03.2017 at point X on 
document Ex. WW1/M1. He further admitted that Ex. WW1/M2, contained his signature at point A which 
is a clearance form dated 31.03.2017. He also admitted that Ex. WW1/M3 was his appointment letter 
dated 02.04.2013, consisting of three pages and was signed by him at point B, C and D. He further 
admitted that his email address was randhirmishra0l1@gmail.com. However, he denied that any memo 


dated 06.05.2016 was sent to him on the email. He further admitted that he had been providing services at a 
company named Delhi Darbar Gastronomy Pvt. Ltd. having its office at 84, Archini, Delhi-1 10030 as an 
electrician. Though he could not recall the exact duration of employment with the company, he stated that 
it was for about 5-6 months. He further admitted that two demand letters dated 09.09.2016 (Ex. WW1/M5 
and WW1/M6) against Delhi Darbar Gastronomy Pvt. Ltd. had been filed by him before the Deputy 
Labour Commissioner, Delhi, wherein he asked for minimum wages and arrears of salary. He, however, 


denied that he had been gainfully employed elsewhere or was providing services to private persons. 


In rebuttal, the management firstly filed the affidavit of Sh. Bharat Bhushan Sharma, however, the 
said witness was substituted by Sh. Trivendra Kumar Sharma. The witness was called for cross- 
examination, but the Ld. AR for the claimant failed to cross-examine the witness despite several 
opportunities and repeated calls by the office of this Tribunal. Consequently, his right of cross-examination 
was closed, and the matter was fixed for final arguments. 


Thereafter, upon a request made on behalf of the claimant, the opportunity to cross-examine the 
management’s witness was reopened, subject to payment of a cost of Rs. 2,000/-. However, the cost was 
not paid, and due to continued non-appearance of the claimant, the right to cross-examine the witness was 
closed again. The testimony of the management’s witness remained unchallenged and unrebutted, and shall 
be read in the evidence. 


The Ld. AR for the claimant failed to appear, to cross-examine the management’s witness despite 
repeated communications from the office of this Tribunal, and also failed to advance final arguments. 
Therefore, this Tribunal was left with no option but to decide the matter in the absence of arguments on 
behalf of the claimant. 


The Ld. AR for the management contended that the present claim is not maintainable, as the 
claimant has not approached the Tribunal with clean hands and has suppressed material facts. It is 
submitted that the claimant did not disclose in his claim statement that he had voluntarily resigned from 


[भाग ए---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7043 


service, and sought to improve his case in the rejoinder by alleging that the resignation was obtained under 
duress and threat to his life. It is further contended that the falsity of the claimant’s case is evident from his 
own admission that he was working with another company during the period of his employment with the 
management. In this regard, reliance is placed upon two demand letters addressed by the claimant to Delhi 
Darbar Gastronomy Pvt. Ltd., wherein he stated that he had been working with the said company w.e.f. 
01.09.2015 as an electrician at a last drawn salary of Rs. 4,000/- per month and claimed unpaid wages of 
Rs. 12,000/-. In the second letter, he alleged non-payment of minimum wages and claimed arrears 
amounting to Rs. 43,392/- for the period from November 2015 to April 2016. 


Upon careful consideration of the pleadings and evidence on record, the issue for determination is 
whether the claim petition is maintainable. The claimant has asserted before this Tribunal that his services 
were illegally terminated by the management on 31.03.2017 and that his wages for the month of March 
2017 were withheld. It is his case that such termination is in violation of Section 25F of the Industrial 
Disputes Act, as neither any notice was served upon him nor was retrenchment compensation paid, as 
mandated under the said provision. 


The claimant’s case is that his service was terminated by the management without assignning any 
reason or giving any prior notice, in violation of Section 25F of the Act. Section 2(00) defines the term 
‘retrenchment’, while Section 25F of the Act sets out the conditions to be complied with by an employer 
before retrenching a workman. The definitions of which are as follows: 


[(00)] “Retrenchment” means the termination by the employer of the service of a 
workman for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment inflicted by way of 
disciplinary action, but does not include— 

(a) voluntary retirement of the workman; or 

(b) retirement of the workman on reaching the age of superannuation if the contract of 
employment between the employer and the workman concerned contains a stipulation in 
that behalf; or 

[(bb)] termination of the service of the workman as a result of the non-renewal of the 
contract of employment between the employer and the workman concerned on its expiry, 
or of such contract being terminated under a stipulation in that behalf contained 
therein; or 


(c) termination of the service of a workman on the ground of continued ill-health. 
Section 25F — Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen: 


No workman employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less 
than one year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until— 

(a) the workman has been given one month’s notice in writing indicating the reasons for 
retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu 
of such notice, wages for the period of the notice; 

(b) the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall 
be equivalent to fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service 
or any part thereof in excess of six months; and 

(c) notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government or such 
authority as may be specified by the appropriate Government by notification in the 
Official Gazette. 


7044 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


From the perusal of the above sections, it is clear that in industrial law, there is no absolute 
protection against retrenchment under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. An employee can be retrenched 
by an employer if certain conditions are fulfilled. The first exception has been provided within the 
definition itself, namely when a workman is terminated by way of disciplinary action. Other exceptions 
include voluntary retirement, superannuation as per contract, non-renewal or termination of a contract on 


its expiry, and termination due to continued ill-health. 


The management has taken the plea that the claimant was in fact not retrenched, and he voluntarily 
tendered his resignation on 30.03.2017 and his resignation was accepted on same date on his request 
because he wanted to join another company and he had been paid full and final amount in lieu of his salary, 
arrears and gratuity on 31.03.2017 itself. 


In this regard, it is important to mention here that the claimant suppressed the material facts from 
this Tribunal. Firstly, he didn’t disclose that he had resigned from the services of the management on 
31.03.2017. Even when he tried to improve his case, he failed to place on record any postal receipt of the 
letter allegedly sent to the management seeking withdrawal of his resignation, meaning thereby that the 
said letter was never actually sent. 


Further, he admitted the fact that he had signed the clearance form dated 31.03.2017 (Ex. 
WW1/M2). He even failed to disclose in his claim statement that he had been working with Delhi Darbar 
Gastronomy Pvt. Ltd., from 06:30 PM to 10:00 PM during the period of his employment with the 
management, and admitted this fact only later in his rejoinder. The plea of part-time employment is also 
falsified because he had claimed minimum wages by sending a demand letter before the conciliation officer 
against Delhi Darbar Gastronomy Pvt. Ltd. (Ex. WW1/M6). 


All these circumstances clearly indicate that the claimant is guilty of suppressing the material facts. 
Moreover, even if the case of the claimant is assumed to be correct, it still falls within the sub-clause (a) of 
section 2(00) of the Act, as the claimant had voluntarily resigned from services. 


In view of the above discussion in hand, the present proceedings are held to be not maintainable, 
and the claimant is not entitled to any relief, much less reinstatement with full back wages. Accordingly, 
the claim of the claimant stands dismissed. A copy of this award be sent to the appropriate government for 
notification under section 17 of the Act. The case file is consigned to record room.

continuing as such the Chief Executive Officer of the Management intimated him by giving a notice 
that his services are no more required by the management and accordingly he was terminated with effect 
from 01.02.2010. His termination of service is not only illegal, unjustified, malafide and arbitrary but also 
against the principle of natural justice. During his tenure of service under the management, neither any 
charge-sheet for misconduct had been made nor any enquiry proceeding had been insisuted against

service as per the provisions of Section 25-B of the I.D. Act and as such he is entitled to get the 
retrenchment compensation and benefits as provided under section 25-F of the I.D. Act.

“8. The learned counsel for the respondent also relied upon a judgment of this Court in W.P. No. 15552 of 
2015 wherein a learned Single Judge of this Court has dismissed a similar Writ Petition filed by the 
workman who challenged the award passed by the Labour Court dismissing the claim statement made by 
the petitioner therein on the ground of delay. After referring to the amended provision, this Court has held 
as follows: 


"The aforesaid provision infers that the workman must raise an industrial dispute before the Conciliation 
Officer and upon expiry of 45 days from the date of filing an application before the Conciliation Officer, 
the workman can move application to the Labour Court before the expiry of three years from the date of his 
dismissal. In any event, right conferred under Section 2A of the Act lapse immediately preceding the date 
of expiry of three years of the date of dismissal. Sub-section (3) of Section 2A operates independently, 
despite the continuation of the conciliation proceeding. While such being the settled provision, in the case 
on hand, the petitioner was dismissed from service on 06.08.2010. Thereafter, after a lapse of 4 years and 2 
months, he filed an application under Section 2A(2) of the 1.0. Act before the Labour Court only on 
31.10.2014. At this juncture, the contention of the petitioner is that he was unable to file an application 
before the Labour Court, since his application filed before the Conciliation Officer was pending. Such 
contention of the petitioner cannot stand to legal scrutiny, for, Sub-Section 3 of Section 2A of the Act 
operates independently, despite the continuation of the conciliation proceedings. Therefore, he ought to 
have filed an application before the learned Labour Court with three years from the date of dismissal order 
passed by the first respondent Corporation on 06.08.2010." 


10. Accordingly, the Writ Petition was dismissed and the order of the Tribunal was confirmed. 


11. The facts of the above case are squarely applicable to the facts of the present case on hand. The 
limitation period prescribed under the provisions of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, is mandatory and this 
Tribunal has no discretion to extend the period of limitation. This fact is established that the Petitioner 
after expiry of three years has preferred the claim petition before this Tribunal on 15.11.2021. Therefore, 
in the light of the above reasons, the claim petition filed by the Petitioner is dismissed merely on the 


ground of being time barred in limini. 
AWARD 


As per discussion above, the claim petition filed by the Petitioner is barred by limitation and the 
same is dismissed accordingly. 


The reference is answered accordingly. 


Record be consigned to the record room.

difference of wages and also paid Annual Bonus / PLRS to Taraknath Bhattacharya on his reversion.

referred to the Office Order dated 18.10.2013 (Exhibit W-2) regarding reversion to original substantive 
post in the non-executive cadre and submitted that in the Office Order, the management has clarified that 
upon reversion of Subordinate Engineers to Non-Executive grade, they are to be treated as if they have not 
been upgraded and pay fixation would be done by associated finance as per rule applicable to Non- 
Executive, allowing benefits relating to NCWA-IX including due increments. It is further argued that till 
date the management has failed to produce any evidence to show that difference of arrear of wages for 
holidays and Sundays, Performance Related Pay (hereinafter referred to as PRP) and Annual Bonus / 


Performance Linked Reward Scheme (hereinafter referred to as PLRS) was paid to the workman. Mr.

Sundays and holidays, Quarterly bonus and Annual bonus. 


10. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL argued that the workman has received 
payment of Rs. 29,838.36/- towards difference of wages between Executive and Non-Executive Cadre 
along with PLRS / Annual Bonus on his reversion. It is submitted that an employee in the Executive Cadre 
is entitled to receive payment for thirty (30) days whereas employees in the Non-Executive Cadre are 
employed for twenty-six (26) days in a month and are entitled to receive payment of wages for only 
twenty-six (26) days, unless he is assigned any duty during Sundays / holidays. Learned advocate for the 
management argued that the workman is not entitled to any payment of wages for Sundays and holidays 
and PLRS / Annual Bonus. 


11. I have considered the arguments advanced on behalf of the management and union, pleadings of 
parties and evidence adduced. It has been admitted by the management that Taraknath Bhattacharya, was 
an employee of ECL, posted at Kunustoria Area and he was promoted to the post of Subordinate Engineer 
(E&M) from the post of Foreman In-charge. I find that the concerned employee was promoted by Office 
Order bearing No. ECL/C-5(D)/Upgradation(E1)/E&M/EE/199 dated 03.02.2011 and he joined his 
promotional post on 02.03.2011 (Exhibit W-2). Thereafter, on his own accord he was reverted to the post 
of Foreman In-charge vide Office Order dated 18.10.2013 (Exhibit M-1/W-2). The Office Order for 
reversion clearly lays down that upon reversion of Subordinate Engineers to Non-Executive grade will be 
treated as if they have not been upgraded and pay fixation will be done by associated finance as per rule 
applicable for non-executives including benefits relating to NCWA-IX, considering due increments. It is 
sufficiently clear that the service of the concerned employee in the post of Foreman in-charge would 
continue as if he was never upgraded to the post of executive and the workman will receive the benefits of 
his increments and pay as per provisions of NCWA-IX. It is an admitted fact that after reversion of 
Taraknath Bhattacharya to the Non-Executive Cadre an amount of Rs.29,838.36/- was paid to him as 
difference of wages. No Calculation Sheet has been produced to show that the concerned workman was 
entitled to the said amount only. According to the clarification provided in the order of reversion the 
workman is entitle to receive his pay as per rules applicable to the Non-Executive Cadre, considering due 
increments, as if they have not been upgraded. It implies that the aggrieved workman is entitle to the 
difference of Basic pay and Dearness Allowance with Quarterly and Annual bonus as a non-executive for 
the period he served in the Executive Cadre from 02.03.2011 to 31.10.2013. An employee in the Non- 
Executive Cadre is employed for twenty-six (26) days a month under usual circumstances. He is employed 
during holidays and Sundays only on special requirement for such deployment. On the other hand, while 
the workman was serving in the promotional post as a Subordinate Engineer, he was employed on all thirty 
(30) days of a month for which he received pay for 30 days. Therefore, the workman is not entitled to any 
payment of Sundays and holidays as a member of the Non-Executive Cadre. His claim for payment of 
difference of wages for eighty-nine (89) holidays during the period he served in the Executive Cadre is not 
tenable. The management however has not produced any documentary evidence in support of their claim 
that PRP and PLRS has been paid to the workman after his reversion to the Non-Executive Cadre for the 
period he served in the Executive Cadre. Since the workman is entitled to receive his dues as a non- 
executive for the period from 02.03.2011 to 31.10.2013, the management shall calculate the difference of 
his Basic pay and Dearness Allowance between the Non-Executive Cadre and Executive Cadre for twenty- 
six (26) days a month without taking into account the payment made for thirty (30) days as executive and

That the Industrial Dispute is allowed in part on contest against the management of Kunustoria

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of

SCHEDULE 


“ Whether the action of the management of Madhaipur Colliery of Pandeveshwar Area, M/s.

1. On receiving Order No. L-22012/92/2022-IR(CM-ID) dated 31.10.2022 from the Government of 
India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 
01.11.2022 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them

2. Mr. Chandi Banerjee, General Secretary, Colliery Mazdoor Union (INTUC) field written statement 
on behalf of the workman on 17.07.2023. The fact of the case as disclosed in the written statement of the 
union is that Shyamal Kumar Roy, Ex-Foreman In-charge of Madhaipur Colliery was promoted to the 
post of Subordinate Engineer (E&M) in the Executive Cadre E-1 in the year 2011 on the basis of Order 
bearing No. ECL/C-5(D)/Upgradation(E1)/E&M/EE/925 dated 21.05.2011 and was posted at Pandaveswar 
Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL). As the workman was suffering 
financial loss due to his upgradation and received less Basic pay than what he was receiving as non- 
executive in the post of Foreman In-charge, he applied for his reversion. The management agreed to revert 
Shyamal Kumar Roy to the post of Foreman In-charge by passing Order bearing No. ECL/C- 
5(D)/Order/Revert Back/E&M/EE/2499 dated 18.10.2013 and he joined as a Foreman In-charge on 
01.11.2013. In the said Order it was clearly mentioned that upon reversion of Subordinate Engineers 
(Mining) to non-executive cadre they would be treated as if they have not been upgraded and pay fixation 
would be done as per rules applicable for non-executives, including benefits under National Coal Wage 
Agreement — IX (hereinafter referred to as NCWA-IX) and would be allowed increments. It is claimed that 
Shyamal Kumar Roy is entitled to get difference of wages, wages for Sundays and holidays as if he was a 
non-executive. In support of his claim the union cited the case of Mr. Apurba Kumar Roy and Mr. Ushapati 
Samanta to whom the management had paid the difference of wages and other consequential benefits on 
their reversion from executive cadre to non-executive cadre. It is the grievance of the union that the 
management of ECL has not paid the difference of wages, wages for Sundays and holidays and prayed for 


passing necessary order. 


7110 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


3. Management of ECL contested the case by filing written statement on the same date i.e., 
06.02.2023. According to the management Shyamal Kumar Roy, Ex-Foreman In-charge of Madhaipur 
Colliery bearing U.M. No. 344066 was upgraded to the post of Subordinate Engineer (E&M) in the 
Executive Cadre ४-1 from the post of Foreman In-charge, vide Order bearing No. ECL/C- 
5(D)/Upgradation(E1)/E&M/EE/925 dated 21.05.2011 issued by the Chief General Manager (P/EE). After 
accepting the terms and conditions of employment Shyamal Kumar Roy was upgraded to the post of 
Executive Cadre E-1. Subsequently, a prayer was made by Shyamal Kumar Roy for reverting him to his 
previous post of Foreman In-charge. Management agreed and reverted him back to his earlier post on 
condition that on reversion the above Subordinate Engineers will be governed by rules and regulations as 
applicable to the non-executive cadre employees and their pay in non-executive grade would be fixed as 
per rules applicable in the earlier non-executive grade held by them prior to upgradation. Management 
asserted that during the period he worked as an executive, he drew salary for thirty (30) days in place of 
twenty-six (26) days payable to a non-executive. The management asserted that the claim of Shyamal 
Kumar Roy as disclosed in written statement by the union is not maintainable and the Industrial Dispute is 
liable to be dismissed. 


4. The dispute referred before this Tribunal for adjudication is whether the action management of 
Madhaipur Colliery under Pandaveswar Area in non-payment of arrears of wages and other consequential 
benefits such as wages for Sundys and holidays to Shyamal Kumar Roy is just and proper. If not, what 
relief the workman is entitled to. 


5. During evidence Shyamal Kumar Roy has been examined as Workman Witness No. 1. He filed the 
following documents : 


(i) Copy of the Office Order dated 05.02.2011 by which Shyamal Kumar Roy was upgraded 
to Executive Cadre E-1, is produced as Exhibit W-1. 


(ii) Copy of the Office Order dated 22.02.2011 by which Shyamal Kumar Roy was posted as 
Subordinate Engineer (E&M) at Pandaveswar Area, as Exhibit W-2. 


(iii) | Copy of Order dated 28.10.2013 / 01.11.2023 by which Shyamal Kumar Roy was reverted 
to his original substantive post in the Non-Executive Cadre, as Exhibit W-3. 


(iv) | Copy of Charge Assumption Report of Shyamal Kumar Roy dated 14.01.2014 by which he 
assumed the charge of Foreman In-charge upon reversion, as Exhibit W-4. 


(v) Copies of three Pay slips of Shyamal Kumar Roy for the months of February, 2014, 
September, 2011 and December, 2013 after reversion to the post of Sr. Overman, as 
Exhibits W-5, W-6 and W-7 respectively. 


During his evidence the witness deposed that on his promotion to the post of Subordinate Engineer (E&M) 
in the Executive Cadre E-1 his Pay Scale was fixed at Rs.16,400/- to Rs.40,500/- by Office Order dated 
05.02.2011. Witness also stated that he is also entitled to employee’s contribution regarding Provident 
Fund deduction over less drawn amount of his wages. 


6. In course of cross-examination the witness deposed that he was posted in the Executive Cadre from 
22.02.2011 till 13.01.2014. He denied that he is not entitled to wages for Sundays and holidays on being 
reverted to the post of Foreman In-charge. 


7. Management examined Mr. Sashiraj Singh, Personnel Manager, Madhaipur Colliery as 
Management Witness No. 1. The witness filed his affidavit-in-chief and stated that Shyamal Kumar Roy 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7111 


was promoted to the post of Subordinate Engineer (E&M) in the Executive Cadre E-1 in the year 2011. 
The aggrieved workman thereafter applied for his reversion to his earlier post and the management passed 
an order for his reversion. It is stated by the witness that the management agreed to fix the pay on reversion 
as per rules and regulations applicable to the non-executive employees. Witness deposed that the 
workman applied for payment of Performance Related Payment (hereinafter referred to as PRP) in lieu of 
arrears / difference of wages for the period he worked in the Executive Cadre, which is under consideration 
as per Office Memorandum circulated vide letter No. CIL/General Manager(P)/B-163 dated 13.03.2018. 
Witness finally stated that there is no question of payment of wages for Sundays and holidays and the 
action of the management is justified. In his evidence-in-chief the management witness further stated that 
there is a difference in the pay between the executive and non-executive cadre as the rules relating to the 
pay of non-executive employees are governed by NCWA which are revised every five years but for 
executive employees the revision is done through Pay Commission Report issued every ten (10) years by 
the Central Government, which is applicable to all the Public Sector Undertaking of the Central 
Government. In course of his evidence management witness produced the following documents : 


(i) | Copy of the Order dated 06/12.09.2013 issued by the General Manager (Personnel), Coal 
India Limited by which the enlisted Executives were reverted back to Non-Executive 
Cadre is produced as_ Exhibit M-1. 


(11) | Copy of the Office Order dated 05.09.2013, as Exhibit M-2. 
(i11) Copy of the Office Memorandum dated 13.03.2018, as Exhibit M-3. 


8. In cross-examination the management witness deposed that he has no knowledge if other reverted 
employee in any other Colliery under ECL was paid difference of wages. The witness denied the 
suggestion that concerned workman is entitled to get difference of Basic, Dearness Allowance, quarterly 
bonus, yearly profit sharing bonus, pay for holidays for the period the workman served in the Executive 
Cadre. 


9. Mr. Chandi Banerjee, union representative, advancing his argument on behalf of the workman 
referred to the Office Order passed by the Chief Manager (Personnel), Pandaveswar Area on 28.10.2013 / 
01.11.2013 (Exhibit W-3) regarding exercise of irrevocable option by the interested Subordinate Engineer 
(E&M) for their reversion to the post in the non-executive cadre and submitted that in the Office Order the 
management has clarified that upon reversion of Subordinate Engineers to Non-Executive grade, they are 
to be treated as if they have not been upgraded and pay fixation would be done by associated finance as per 
tule applicable to Non-Executive including benefits relating to NCWA-IX including due increments. Mr. 
Banerjee argued that upon reversion Basic pay of the workman was fixed at Rs.45,966.63/- (Exhibit W-5) 
which is much higher than Rs.28,269.91/- fixed as Basic pay in the Executive Cadre ४-1 (Exhibit W-7). 
The union representative submitted that the workman is entitled to payment of Basic pay along with 
Dearmess Allowance during the period he was posted in the Executive Cadre E-1, from 22.02.2011 to 
13.01.2014 as per rules with benefits admissible under NCWA-IX. Mr. Chandi Banerjee further submitted 
that the workman is entitled to payment of wages during Sundays and holidays and further entitled to get 
quarterly bonus, annual puja bonus. Mr. Banerjee argued that till date and the management has failed to 
produce any evidence to show that PRP has been paid to the workman. 


10. Mr. Mani Padma Banerjee, learned advocate for the management of ECL admitted that the 
workman has not received any payment towards difference of Basic pay, Dearness Allowance, 
Underground Allowance, quarterly bonus, annual puja bonus or PRP. It is argued that a workman is 


7112 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


entitled to receive payment of wages for only twenty-six (26) days a month, unless he is assigned any 
specific duty during holidays. Learned advocate for the management argued that the workman is not 
entitled to any payment of wages for Sundays and holidays. 


11. I have considered the arguments advanced on behalf of the management and union, pleadings of 
parties and evidence adduced. It has been admitted by the management that Shyamal Kumar Roy, U.M. 
No. 344066, was an employee of ECL, posted at Pandaveswar Area and he was promoted to the post of 
Subordinate Engineer (E&M) from the post of Foreman In-charge. On a perusal of the record, I find that 
the concerned employee was promoted by Office Order bearing No. ECL/C- 
5(D)/Upgradation(E1)/E&M/EE/212 dated 05.02.2011 (Exhibit W-1) and he joined his promotional post 
on 22.02.2011 (Exhibit W-2). Thereafter, on his own accord he was reverted to the post of Foreman In- 
charge vide Office Order dated 28.10.2013 / 01.11.2013 (Exhibit W-3). The Office Order for reversion 
(Exhibit W-3) clearly lays down that upon reversion of Subordinate Engineers to Non-Executive grade will 
be treated as if they have not been upgraded and pay fixation will be done by associated finance as per rule 
applicable for non-executives including benefits relating to NCWA-IX considering due increments. It is 
sufficiently clear that the service of the concerned employee in the post of Foreman In-charge would 
continue as if he was never upgraded to the post of executive and the workman will receive the benefits of 
his increments and pay as per provisions of NCWA-IX. From the Pay slip of February 2014, it would 
appear that the upon reversion to the Non-Executive Cadre the Basic Pay of the workman was fixed at 
Rs.45,966.63/- which is higher than the Basic pay of Rs.28,269.91/-, which the workman received in the 
month of December 2013 (Exhibit W-7) while he was posted in the Executive Cadre. Therefore, it is clear 
admission on the part of the management that after reversion, the workman was neither paid any difference 
of wages nor any consequential benefits. Therefore, I find that Shyamal Kumar Roy, the aggrieved 
workman is entitled to receive difference of Basic Pay and Dearness Allowance for the period from 
22.02.2011 to 13.01.2014, as if he was in the post of Foreman In-charge in the non-executive cadre. 


12. The evidence reveals that no PRP has been paid to the employee on his reversion. It should be 
borne in mind that the Industrial Dispute has been raised for non-payment of arrear of wages for the 
aforesaid two (2) years, while the workman was employed in the Executive Cadre E-1. The question of 
payment of different allowances and perks does not arise. As the concerned workman has received 
payments for Sundays and holidays while he served as an executive, he is not entitled to any additional 
payments for Sundays and holidays as a non-executive. A non-executive is generally employed on twenty- 
six (26) days a month. It is not mandatory that workmen in the non-executive cadre would be deployed on 
all Sundays and holidays. Therefore, they are not entitled to any payment for Sundays and holidays. In the 
instant case the workman has not been paid any quarterly bonus and annual puja bonus during his posting 
in the Executive Cadre E-1 for the period from 22.02.2011 to 13.01.2014. The management of Madhaipur 
Colliery under Pandaveswar Area of ECL therefore has acted in and illegal and arbitrary manner by 
withholding the payment of difference of Basic pay and Dearness Allowance as well as Underground 
Allowance, quarterly bonus and annual puja bonus despite clarification made in order dated 05.09.2013 
(Exhibit M-2). I therefore, hold that Shyamal Kumar Roy, U.M. No. 344066 who was reverted to the post 
of Foreman In-charge at Madhaipur Colliery under Pandaveswar Area and has already superannuated from 
service, is entitled to payment of arrears of difference of Basic pay and Dearness Allowance from the 
management of ECL for the period from 22.02.2011 to 13.01.2014 while he was posted as Subordinate 
Engineer (E&M) in the Executive Cadre E-1. He is further entitled to receive Underground Allowance for 
the said period along with quarterly bonus and annual puja bonus for the period. The management of 


[भाग ए---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत HT UAT : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7113 


Pandaveswar Area, ECL is directed to assess the dues payable to Shyamal Kumar Roy within two (2) 
months from the date of communication of the Award and disburse the same without any delay. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


That the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Madhaipur Colliery 
under Pandaveswar Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited. Shyamal Kumar Roy, the aggrieved workman with 
U.M. No. 344066, who is superannuated from the service of Eastern Coalfields Limited as a Foreman In- 
charge in the Non-Executive Cadre is entitled to arrears of difference of Basic pay, Dearness Allowance 
between the Executive Cadre and Non-Executive Cadre for the period from 22.02.2011 to 13.01.2014. He 
shall further be entitled to get Underground Allowance, Quarterly Bonus and Annual Puja Bonus for the 
said period. The management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to assess and disburse the amount 
payable to the aggrieved workman within two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. 
Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the 
Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, New Delhi for information and Notification.

The Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, in exercise of powers conferred under

1947), vide its Order No. L-22012/83/2017-IR(CM-ID) dated 16.11.2017 and Order No. L-22012/83/2017-

Management of Kalipahari Colliery under Sripur Area of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter

SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the Management of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Ltd. in relation to its 
Kalipahari Colliery under Sripur Area in not providing employment to Sri Raju Kora, dependent son of the 
deceased workman Late Sriram Kora, as per National Coal Wage Agreement is justified? If not, to what 


relief the dependent of ex-workman is entitled to? ”. 


1. Initially Order No. L-22012/83/2017 - IR(CM-II) dated 16.11.2017 was received from the 
Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of a dispute and a Reference case 
No. 17 of 2017 was registered on 28.11.2017 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties 
through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant 
documents in support of their claims and a list of witnesses. Thereafter, the same Industrial Dispute with an 
identical schedule was referred to this Tribunal by Order No. L-22012/83/2017 - IR(CM-II) dated 
05.11.2018 which was registered as Reference case No. 35 of 2018. Two cases were registered separately 
and by order dated 31.12.2019 passed in both the cases, bearing Reference No. 35/2018 and 17/2017, they 


were taken up together for disposal. 
2. Koyala Mazdoor Congress representing Raju Kora filed written statement 


on 30.07.2018. The fact of the case in brief, as per written statement of the union is that Sriram Kora was 
an employee of ECL and was posted as Explosive Carrier at Kalipahari Colliery under Sripur Area. He 
died in harness on 18.12.1995. Raju Kora, the dependent son of Sriram Kora submitted an application for 
providing him employment as per the provisions of NCWA. The Colliery authorities after observing all 
formalities forwarded the employment file to the Area office and thereafter it was forwarded to the ECL 
Headquarters. Clarification was sought for by the Agent, Kalipahari Colliery vide his letter No. 
AGT/KPH/C-6D/Employment/08/894 dated 4/9.9.2008. The dependent son replied to the queries and also 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7115 


submitted documents. The employment file was thereafter forwarded to Area level but after passage of 
several years, no decision has been taken by the management nor any employment is provided to the 
dependent son of Sriram Kora on compassionate ground. Several representations had been submitted by the 
dependent son as well as union for finalizing the claim but no action has been taken by the management. 


Hence, the Industrial Dispute is raised through the union claiming employment for Raju Kora. 


3. Management of Kalipahari (R) Colliery contested the case by filing written statement on 
29.11.2022. According to the management, Sriram Kora was an employee of ECL posted at Kalipahri (R) 
Colliery and expired on 18.12.1995. After the death of employee, a claim was preferred for providing 
employment to the dependent of the deceased employee after a gap of 19 years and 6 months from the date 
of death of the employee. In the instant case, there has been inordinate delay in preferring the claim, as 
such the dependent is not entitled to any employment. Further case of the management is that no 
representation was made before them for providing employment to the dependent son. It is contended that 
the action of the management in not providing employment after a delayed claim is justified. The 


management accordingly prayed for dismissing the case. 


4. The relevant issue for consideration is that whether Raju Kora, dependent son of deceased Sriram 
Kora is entitled to the relief of compassionate employment according to the provisions of NCWA and 


whether the action of the management in not providing the employment is justified? 


5. The union examined Raju Kora as WW-1. He filed his affidavit-in-chief averring that after the 
death of his father on 18.12.1995, his mother initially applied for providing employment to her against the 
death of his father as his age was wrongly recorded below 18 years at the time of death of his father. Later 
on the wife of the deceased nominated the son, Raju Kora, for employment as per provisions of NCWA 
and submitted necessary documents. The management of ECL issued letters dated 12.06.2001 for screening 
of the applicant for employment. After screening, the file was forwarded to Area Level and Raju Kora was 
also asked to appear before the IME Board for medical examination by letter No. GM/SA/C-6B/7/2001/D- 
121 dated 13.09.2001. After observing such formalities, management did not communicate anything to the 


dependent son and did not provide any employment. 
During examination-in-chief, the witness produced the following documents: 
(1) Copy of death certificate of Sriram Kora is produced as Exhibit W-1. 


(11) Copy of letter issued by the wife of the deceased employe praying for employment of Raju 
Kora is produced as Exhibit W-2. 


(iii) Copy of letter issued by Area Medical Officer, Sripur Area addressed to Chief Medical 
Officer, Sanctoria Hospital dated 22.10.2001 for holding IME of Raju Kora is produced as 
Exhibit W-3. 


The witness deposed that at the time of his father’s death he was fourteen (14) years of age. In cross-

9. I have considered the facts and circumstances of the case disclosed in the pleadings of the parties, 
evidence adduced and arguments advanced on behalf of both parties. Admittedly, Sriram Kora was an 
employee of ECL and he died in harness on 18.12.1995. At the time of death of employee, his son Raju

has stated that he was 14 years of age at the time of death of his father. He also deposed that he was unable 
to produce any document in support of his date of birth. Initially, an attempt was made by Raju Kora to 
assert that his age was wrongly recorded as below 18 years in the office records of his father but the 
witness was unable to prove that he was a major at that time. From the report of IME (Exhibit M-3), I find 
that Raju Kora disclosed his age as 22 years on 08.11.2001. On the basis of such statement, his age maybe 
computed as 16 years at the time of his father’s death. The NCWA-V was published on 22.02.1996. In the 
circular bearing No. CIL/JBCCI-V/I.I.NO.(8/96)/2627 dated 22.02.1996, it has been stated that the 
provision for keeping the name of minor dependents in the live roster for the purpose of employment under 
clause 9.4.0 of NCWA-V will be effective from the date of issue the order 1.6. 22.02.1996. It needs to be 
borne in mind that the provisions relating to compassionate employment to dependents emanates out of 
negotiated agreements arrived at between the employer and employee which is treated as a settlement 
under section 2(p) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and it has a binding effect on the parties under 
section 18 (3) of the Industrial Disputes Act of 1947. The provisions for compassionate employment for the 
dependents of the deceased have been made in NCWA-V but the same is applicable only prospectively 
from 22.02.1996 and not retrospectively from 01.07.1991. It seems that the management of ECL carried 
out a futile exercise by holding screening and IME of Raju Kora and also declaring him fit for underground 
job. The management ought to have acted in accordance with the provisions of NCWA-IV before giving 
false hopes to the suffering dependents. 


10. Under the facts and circumstances of this case, Raju Kora, the dependent 


son of Sriram Kora is not entitled to employment under the provisions of NCWA applicable at the time of 
death of his father. The Industrial Dispute is therefore dismissed on contest

entitled to the benefit of both Executive and Non-Executive Cadres and the management is totally justified 
in not paying arrears of wages to the concern employee and he is not entitled to get any relief. In course of 
evidence management witness has produced a Calculation sheet (Exhibit M-1) signed by the Dy. Manager 
(Fin), Kunustoria Colliery and the Asst. Manager (HR), Kunustoria Colliery. The witness deposed that 
according to the Calculation sheet (Exhibit M-1) difference of gross pay after reversion is recoverable from 
the workman. On a perusal of the Calculation sheet, it appears that an amount of Rs.1,02,045.81/- is the 
difference of pay which the workman has received in excess as an executive. In course of cross- 
examination the management witness admitted that the management has included amounts towards leave 
encashment paid to the workman in August 2013 due to which the gross amount paid in the Executive 
Cadre has been shown as Rs.1,51,262.75/-. In a similar manner the column showing the payment as an 
executive also includes leave encashment paid in the month of August 2011 which is Rs.85,122,63/-. A 
suggestion was put to the management witness that the Calculation sheet produced is without any basis. On 
a close scrutiny of the Calculation sheet, I find that it is totally flawed and does not specify separate heads 
of payment in the Executive and Non-Executive Cadres. In order to give a proper effect to the clarification 
that upon reversion from Executive to Non-Executive Cadre the workman would be treated as if they have 
not been upgraded, it would be incumbent upon the management of ECL to assess the difference of Basic 
pay and Dearmess allowance between the pay received in the Executive Cadre and the pay to which the 
workman is entitled as non-executive, only in respect of twenty-six (26) working days. While assessing 
such difference of pay the management cannot take into consideration the payment made to the workman, 
as an executive for thirty (30) days a month as his pay for twenty-six (26) days as non-executive has to be 
taken into consideration. It is also to be noted that the leave encashment are separate entities which is not a 
component of regular pay and cannot be taken into consideration at the time of assessing the difference of 
Basic pay and Dearness allowance for twenty-six (26) days each month. Furthermore, the management 
cannot take into consideration other allowance paid to the workman as an executive to calculate the gross 
payment of wages made to him while he was posted as an executive. There is no averment in the written 
statement that management has paid any PRP to the workman during the period of his deployment in the 
Executive Cadre. Therefore, the concerned workman on his reversion is also entitled to his Quarterly and 
Annual bonus during the period from 12.02.2011 to 31.10.2013.

dues in the light of my observation and make payment of arrears of difference of Basic pay and Dearness 
allowance along with Quarterly and Annual bonus within two (2) months from the date of communication 
of the Award.

the difference of wages and other consequential benefits on their reversion from executive cadre to non-

After accepting the terms and conditions of employment Tarun Kumar Ghosal was upgraded to the post of

Subsequently, a prayer was made by the employee for reverting him to his previous post of Senior

and the Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


4. The dispute referred to this Tribunal for adjudication is whether the management of 
Shyamsundarpur Colliery has paid the arrears of difference of wages, Dearness Allowance, wages for

In course of his evidence the witness deposed that his Basic pay was fixed at Rs.25,870.96/- w.e.f.

aggrieved workman thereafter applied for his reversion to the earlier post and the management passed

8. In cross-examination the management witness deposed that in the Calculation Sheet payments

that the concerned workman is entitled to get difference of Basic pay, Dearness Allowance, Underground

9. Mr. Chandi Banerjee, advancing his argument on behalf of the workman referred to the order 
passed by the management on 18.10.2013 and 21.10.2013 regarding exercise of irrevocable option by the 
interested Subordinate Engineer (Mining) for their reversion to the post in the non-executive cadre. It is 
submitted that in the later Office Order dated 18/20.11.2013 the management has clarified that “Upon 
reversion of SOE to Non-Executive grade will be treated as if they have not been upgraded and pay 
fixation will be done by associated finance as per rule applicable for Non-Executive including benefits 
relating to NCWA-IX considering due increments”. It is asserted that Office Order dated 21.10.2013 
(Exhibit W-2) provided that upon reversion of Subordinate Engineer (Mining) to non-executive, would be 
treated as if they have not been upgraded. Mr. Banerjee argued that upon reversion Basic pay of the 
workman was fixed at Rs.43,766.66/- (Exhibit W-5 / W-6) which is much higher than the Basic pay 
Rs.25,870.96/- in the Executive Cadre E-1 (Exhibit W-3). The union representative submitted that the 
workman is entitled to difference of payment of Basic pay along with Dearness Allowance for the period 
he was posted in the Executive Cadre E-1 from 16.03.2011 to 31.10.2013 as per rules with benefits 
admissible under NCWA-IX. It is further submitted that the workman is entitled to payment of wages for

Sundays and holidays and further entitled to quarterly bonus and annual puja bonus. Referring to admission 
of Management Witness No. 1 in his cross-examination, it is argued that the concerned workman though 
entitled to get difference of wages, Dearness Allowance, quarterly bonus and annual puja bonus, no 
payment has been paid till date and the management has failed to adduce any evidence to show that PRP 
has been made to the workman. 


10. Mr. P. K. Goswami, learned advocate for ECL admitted the fact that the management of ECL has 
not paid any difference of wages, Dearness Allowance, Underground Allowance, quarterly bonus and 
annual puja bonus to the aggrieved workman. It is argued that a workman is entitled to receive payment for 
only twenty-six (26) days a month, unless he is assigned any duty during holidays. Learned advocate for 
the management argued that the workman is not entitled to any payment for Sundays and holidays. 


11. I have considered the arguments advanced on behalf of the management of ECL and the union, 
pleadings of parties and evidence adduced. It is admitted by management that Tarun Kumar Ghosal, U.M. 
No. 550723, was an employee of ECL at Bankola Area and he was promoted to the post of Subordinate 
Engineer (Mining) from the post of Senior Overman. The concerned employee joined his promotional post 
on 16.03.2011 and on his own seeking was reverted to the post of Senior Overman on 01.11.2013. the 
order of reversion (Exhibit W-2) clearly lays down that upon reversion from Executive Cadre ४-1 to non- 
executive cadre they would be treated as if they were not upgraded and pay fixation would be done by 
Associated Finance as per rule applicable to non-executive, including benefits relating to NCWA-IX 
considering due increments. It is sufficiently clear that the service of the concerned employee in the post of 
Senior Overman continued as if he was never been upgraded to the post of executive and the workman is 
entitled to receive the benefits of his increments and pay as per provisions of NCWA-IX. From the Pay 
slips for the months November, 2013 and December, 2013 (Exhibit W-5 and W-6) it would appear that the 
Basic Pay of the workman was fixed at Rs.43,766.66/- which is higher than the Basic pay of 
Rs.25,870.96/-, which the workman received on his upgradation from 16.03.2011. Therefore, it is a clear 
admission on the part of the management that after reversion, neither difference of wages nor consequential 
benefits was paid to the workman. Therefore, I find that Tarun Kumar Ghosal, the aggrieved workman is 
entitled to get difference of Basic Pay and Dearness Allowance for the period from 16.03.2011 to 
31.10.2013, as if he was in the post of Senior Overman in the non-executive cadre. 


12. The evidence reveals that no PRP has been paid to the employee on his reversion. In the 
Calculation Sheet (Exhibit M-2) I find that the Basic pay of the workman in the non-executive cadre has 
been fixed as Rs.42,066.01/- and the Basic pay which he has received in the Executive Cadre E-1 for the 
same month was Rs.26,647.08/-. It is therefore, clear that there had been revision of pay for the non- 
executive employees from July, 2011 and the aggrieved workman has not received the difference of 
payment. It should be borne in mind that the Industrial Dispute has been raised for non-payment of Basic 
pay and Dearness Allowance for the aforesaid two (2) years, while the workman was employed in the 
Executive Cadre E-1. The question of payment of different allowances and perks does not arise as the 
concerned workman has received payments for Sundays and holidays while he served as an executive but 
he is not entitled to any additional payments for Sundays and holidays as a non-executive. A non-executive 
employee is generally employed on twenty-six (26) days a month. It is not mandatory that workmen in the 
non-executive cadre would be deployed on all Sundays and holidays unless a requisition is made. 
Therefore, they are not entitled to any payment for Sundays and holidays. In the instant case the workman 
has not been paid any quarterly bonus and annual puja bonus during his posting in the Executive Cadre E-1 
for the period from 16.03.2011 to 31.10.2013. I therefore, find and hold that the management of

Shyamsundarpur Colliery under Bankola Area of ECL has acted in and illegal and arbitrary manner by 
withholding the legitimate dues of difference of Basic pay and Dearness Allowance as well as

No. 550723, who was reverted to the post of Senior Overman at Shyamsundarpur Colliery under Bankola 
Area and already superannuated from service is entitled to payment of arrears of difference of Basic pay 
and Dearness Allowance from the management of ECL for the period from 16.03.2011 to 31.10.2013 while 
he was posted as Subordinate Engineer (Mining) in the Executive Cadre E-1. He is further entitled to 
Underground Allowance for the said period along with quarterly bonus and annual puja bonus for the

The facts giving rise to the present reference in gist are that Electronics Regional Test Laboratory

establishment had floated a tender for engagement of security guards.One M/s. Dikarton, being the lowest

in the establishment of the principal employer for more than ten years through M/s. Dikarton. That without 
their knowledge the contract between the principal employer and the contractor was revoked in the month 
of October, 1999. That after the contract of M/s. Dikarton was expired, the principal employer retained the 
concerned eight security guards till 29-11-2000 and paid their wages, but suddenly without any notice their

when M/s.Dikarton withdrew the contract during the subsistence of the contract. He has further stated that 
the establishment still has six security guards and which are provided by the service provider enlisted in the 
GEM Portal. That they have no occasion to engage or terminate the concerned eight security guards. 


Documents which have come on record prima facie shows that Electronics Regional Test 
Laboratory (East), Kolkata being a Central Govt. establishment had procured the services of security 
guards at its establishment through tender process. Itaccepted the tender of M/s. Dikarton being the lowest 
bidder. M/s. Dikarton being the security agency has provided those eight security guards in the 
establishment of principal employer and which has also been admitted by the W.W. No.1 in his cross 
examination. Thus, prima facie it is seen that eight concerned workmen were the employees of M/s. 
Dikarton and not the employees of Electronics Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata. 


From Exhibit M-3 dated 20-08-2000 it is seen that M/s. Dikarton had written to the Director of 
Electronics Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata informing its inability to continue the contract of 
supply of security guards due to circumstances beyond its control beyond the month of September, 2000. It 
further reveals that M/s. Dikarton was rendering security services to the establishment of Electronics 
Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata for last ten years. Exhibit-M-4 shows that Joint Director (Admn.) 
of Electronics Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata had accepted the prayer of M/s. Dikarton for 
midterm termination of its contact and permitted to provide security guards till the end of September, 2000. 


Copy of orders passed in the Writ Petitionthough not exhibited but admitted by W.W. No.1 in his 
cross examination about moving Hon’ble High Court in writ jurisdiction for redressal of their 
grievances.Such orders passed by Hon’ble High Court prima facie shows that those eight security guards 
moved Hon’ble High Court by filing a writ petition in the month of August, 2000. After hearing the parties 
the Hon’ble High Court was pleased to direct the parties to maintain status quo in respect of the writ 
petitioners i.e. concerned workmen’s services on that day for a period till one week after puja vacation. 
Order dated 20-11-2000 passed by the Hon’ble High Court shows that the status quo order passed on 297 
September, 2000 stands vacated and cannot direct M/s. Dikarton to keep the petitioners in service. The said 
writ petition no. 16998 (W) of 20000 was finally disposed of in the month of January, 2002 and from 
which it appears there was an order on 24 September, 2000 directing the parties to maintainstatusquo in 
respect of the petitioners’ services. It was submitted on 297 September, 2000 the petitioners were in service 
and they remained in service till 247 November,2000 and as such directed the Electronics Regional Test 
Laboratory (East), Kolkata to pay salary/wages to the petitioners for the aforesaid period only with liberty 
to recover the same if it has been paid to their concerned contractoron account of their salary/wages during 
the period. 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7133 


From such orders passed by the Hon’ble High Court, it appears that eight concerned workmen 
were well aware of the Exhibit-M-3, letter dated 20-08-2000 of M/s. Dikarton to the Director of 
Electronics Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata for withdrawal of its service contract and permitting 
it to provide security guards till 30" September,2000. That Exhibit M-4 shows that the authority of 
Electronics Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata had accepted the request for termination of the 
contract of M/s. Dikarton by issuing a letter dated 21-09-2000 and permitted them to provide security 
guards till 300 September 2000 and as such they had moved the Hon’ble High Court. From the orders 
passed by the Hon’ble High Court, it appears that services of those security guards of M/s. Dikarton 
wereretained by Electronics Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata till 24™November, 2000 and 
Electronics Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata was directed to pay wages to those eight concerned 
security guards for the period from October, 2000 to 247 November, 2000. So, it is seen that Electronics 
Regional Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata never retained the services of those eight security guards after the 
termination of the contract it had with M/s. Dikarton but had to retain the services of those eight security 
guards till 247 November,2000 as per the order and direction of the Hon’ble High Court and had to pay 
wages to them as per order of the Hon’ble High Court. 


Such very facts also prove that those eight workmen were never engaged by Electronics Regional 
Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata after the withdrawal of contractby M/s. Dikarton, rather it was compelled 
to retain those eight security guards of its ex-contractor and pay them wages for the period they were 
retained by it in compliance of the order and direction given by the Hon’ble High Court at Calcutta. 


Further, from the Annexure-7 it is seen Reference Case No. 8 of 2005 was initiated in this Tribunal 
by virtue of receipt of order No. L-42012/322/2003 IR (CM-II) dated 28-12-2004 from theCentral Govt., 
Ministry of Labour vide which following dispute was referred for adjudication: - 


“Whether Sri Bidyut Kumar Biswas and seven others, Security Guards in the Estt. Of Electronics 
Regional Test Laboratory (East),, Deptt. of Information Technology, STQC Directorate, Kolkata are 
entitled for regularisation of their service in the organisation? If yes, to what relief they are entitled?” 


Such reference was culminated in no dispute award passed by the predecessor of this Tribunal on 
10-03-2008 and from such award it is seen present eight concerned workmen had filed a petition praying 
for passing no dispute award and accordingly such reference case was ended in no dispute award. Such 
very facts also prove the concerned workmen were not directly engaged by Electronics Regional Test 
Laboratory (East), Kolkata. 


In view of the above, the issue under reference become redundant and infructuous. Further, nothing 
has come on record to prove that the contract between M /s. Dikarton and Electronics Regional Test 
Laboratory (East), Kolkata with regard to the employment of Sri Bidyut Kumar Biswas and seven others is 
sham and bogus. In fact, the services of those security guards had come to an end with the termination of 
the contract between the principal employer and the contractor employer.Since they being employees on 
contract, their services cannot be deemed to be terminated by the principal employer Electronics Regional 
Test Laboratory (East), Kolkata on 24-11-2000 and their service cannot be deemed to be continued after 
the termination of the contract between their immediate employer and the principal employer. Therefore, 
the Reference is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed. 


In view of the above the Reference Case No. 03/2010 is disposed of with dismissal award. 


K. D. BHUTIA, Presiding Officer

The present reference has been made by the Central Government by its order No. L- 
42012/2/25/2021(IR(DU) dated 22/2/2023 passed in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (d) of sub- 
section (1) and sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the Industrial Dispute Act 1947. The terms of reference 
as per the schedule to the said order are as under: 


“Whether Whether dispute raised by Sh. Achyut Vishwanath Irpe vide letter dated 23.2.2021 
against the management of M/s. B4S Solutions Pvt. Ltd, Pune for alleged illegal transfer from 


Latur to Pune is covered under the Industrial Dispute under the jurisdiction of the Central 


7144 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : JULY 18, 2026/ASHADHA 27, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


Government under ID Act, 1947? If yes, whether the action of the management of M/s. b4S 
Solutions Pvt. Ltd., Pune to transfer Sh. Achyut Vishwanath Irpe from Latur to Pune is proper, 
legal and justified? If not, to what relief the concerned applicant is entitled to? What direction, if 


any, is necessary in the matter?” 


In view of the above said facts the claimant/workman has not filed any statement of claim/ evidence in 
support of his case on affidavit, in spite of several opportunities given to him and taking into consideration 
the law as laid by the Hon'ble High Court in the case of V. K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court (1) and 
others 1981 (29) FLR 194 as under: 


“It is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to prove 
illegality of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the Court must fail. 
Whenever a workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of service if is imperative 
for him to file written statement before the Industrial Court setting out grounds on which the order is 
challenged and he must also produce evidence to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file 
written statement or produce evidence, the dispute referred by the State Government cannot be answered 


in favour of the workman and he would not be entitled to any relief.” 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding 
Officer, Labour Court (II), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (118) FLR 1164 Hon’ble Allahabad High Court 
has held as under: 


“The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., 
V.K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1984 (49) 
FLR 38 and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led 
by or on behalf of the workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In 
such a situation it is not necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead 
evidence to establish an allegation made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would 


be, who would fail if no evidence is led.” 


And by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. 
P.A.C.C.S.C. Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co-operative Bank Ltd. 2010 (126) FLR 519; 


Management submits as under:- 


1. The Second Party workman Sh. Achyut Vishwanath Irpe has tendered his resignation from the services 
of the First Party Company with effect from 30/3/2021. 


2. The Second Party workman also has submitted a letter dated 5/6/2023 in which he has informed the First 
Party that he is withdrawing the Industrial Dispute bearing No. Reference CGIT 24 of 2023 which is 
pending adjudication in this Hon’ble Tribunal, he has stated in said letter that he would be filing 
application to this effect before this Hon’ble Tribunal within 14 days. 


3. Even otherwise the Second Party workman had remained absent with effect from 20" October 2020 to 
7" April 2023. His name therefore was removed from the services of the company on 07" April 2023 on 
ground that he had abandoned his services. A copy of letter dated 077" April 2023 issued by First Party 
Company to Second Party workman is annexed with this application Now in view of the resignation by 
Second Party, Second Party’s discharge stands converted to acceptance of resignation. 


4. The First Party employer therefore state and submits that no cause of action survives in the Industrial 
Dispute now and the adjudication proceedings in this case become infructuous. 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : जुलाई, 18/आषाढ, 27,1948 7145

want of cause of action. 


Since no statement of claim has been filed by the workman in support of his case, the claim is liable to be 
dismissed. 


For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and the workman is not entitled for any relief.

(hereinafter called as Act) against his termination dated 03.06.2014 claiming reinstatement in service 
with continuity of service along with full back wages. 


File taken up in special campaign for disposal of pending cases. Workman along with his AR and AR 


for management made the following joint statement:- 
Stated that both the parties agreed to settle the dispute on the following terms:- 


1. That the Panjab University is ready to reinstate the workman Hardeep Singh on DC rates with 


the same terms and conditions at the time of earlier appointment with continuity of service. 


2. That this settlement will not provide in any immunity in case after joining he commits any de- 


relaxation of duty in future. 


3. That the workman will not claim any wages/compensation for the period he remained out of 


employment during the pendency of this case. 


In view of the above statement, the workman Hardeep Singh would be reinstated with the 
management on DC rates with the same terms and conditions at the time of earlier appointment with 


continuity of service. Parties shall be bound by the statement of their AR. 


Let copy of this award be sent to the Appropriate Government as required under Section 17 of the Act 
for publication.

कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने 
का अनुरोध किया है।

4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था

G.S.R. 34.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal, Staff Car Driver Recruitment Rules, 984; the Income-tax 
Appellate Tribunal (Group ‘C’ Posts) Recruitment Rules, 984, in so far as they relate to the post of the Stenographer 
Grade III; the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal, Multi-Tasking Staff, Group ‘C’ Post Recruitment Rules, 205; the 
Income-tax Appellate Tribunal, Clerical Group ‘C’ Posts Recruitment Rules, 209, except as respects things done or 
omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of 
recruitment to the posts of Upper Division Clerk, Stenographer Grade II, Lower Division Clerk, Staff Car Driver and 
Multi-Tasking Staff, in the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal, namely :- 


l. Short title and commencement.— (l) These rules may be called the Income-tax Appellate Tribunal (Group ‘C’ 
Posts) Recruitment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the official Gazette. 


2. Application.- These rules shall apply to the posts as specified in column (l) of the Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 
3. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix.- The number of the said posts, their classification 


and level in the pay matrix attached to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule. 


4. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (3) of the said Schedule. 


3. Disqualification.- No person,-

be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the ex-Servicemen and 
other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time 
in this regard.

S.O. 498.—Whereas by a notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Steel and 
S.O.No.l095(E) dated 257 February 2026, issued under sub-section (l) of section 3 of the Petroleum and 
Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 962 (50 of 962) (hereinafter referred to as 
the said Act), published in the Extra Ordinary Gazette of India dated the 270 February 2026, the Central 
Government declared its intention to acquire the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule 
appended to that notification for the purpose of laying pipeline for the transportation of Iron Ore in the 
form of slurry from Kirandul to Visakhapatnam through the State of Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra 
Pradesh by M/s. ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India Private Limited. 


And whereas the Competent Authority has under sub-section (l) of section 6 of the said Act, 


submitted report to the Central Government. 


And whereas the Central Government, after considering the said report, decided to acquire the 


right of user in the lands specified in the Schedule appended to this notification. 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) section 6 of the said Act, the 
Central Government hereby declares that the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule appended to 


this notification is hereby acquired for laying pipelines. 


And further in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of said section 6, the Central 


Government hereby directs that the right of user in the lands specified in the Schedule appended to this

S.O. 499.—Whereas by a notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Steel and 
S.O.No.l094(E) dated 25 February 2026, issued under sub-section (l) of section 3 of the Petroleum and 
Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 962 (50 of 962) (hereinafter referred to as 
the said Act), published in the Extra Ordinary Gazette of India dated the 27" February 2026, the Central 
Government declared its intention to acquire the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule 
appended to that notification for the purpose of laying pipeline for the transportation of Iron Ore in the 
form of slurry from Kirandul to Visakhapatnam through the State of Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra 
Pradesh by M/s. ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India Private Limited. 


And whereas the Competent Authority has under sub-section (l) of section 6 of the said Act, 
submitted report to the Central Government. 


And whereas the Central Government, after considering the said report, decided to acquire the 
right of user in the lands specified in the Schedule appended to this notification. 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) section 6 of the said Act, the 
Central Government hereby declares that the right of user in the land specified in the Schedule appended to 
this notification is hereby acquired for laying pipelines. 


And further in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of said section 6, the Central 
Government hereby directs that the right of user in the lands specified in the Schedule appended to this 
notification shall instead of vesting in the Central Government vest on the date of publication of this 
declaration in M/s. ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India Private Limited, free from all encumbrances.
